skills.name: design-trade-study
skills.desc: Compare bounded parametric kernelCAD design variants on one evidence basis. Use for “compare options,” “optimize this design,” “which variant is best,” or a make-versus-design decision. Computes comparable metrics, shows evidence for and against each candidate, runs sensitivity analysis, and keeps the selected variant behind a human review gate.
skills.body:
---
name: design-trade-study
description: >-
  Compare bounded parametric kernelCAD design variants on one evidence basis. Use for “compare options,” “optimize this design,” “which variant is best,” or a make-versus-design decision. Computes comparable metrics, shows evidence for and against each candidate, runs sensitivity analysis, and keeps the selected variant behind a human review gate.
---

# Design trade study

A trade study is not “generate several shapes and choose the nicest.” It is a
controlled comparison where every candidate uses the same requirements, units,
revision base, and scoring rule.

Read `references/evidence-contract.md` and
`references/scoring-and-sensitivity.md` before starting.

## Workflow

1. **Freeze the baseline.** Fetch the exact saved revision with
   `get_project_revision`, or hash the exact inline source. Preserve the
   baseline unchanged.
2. **Define the decision.** Record the hard constraints, metrics, direction of
   preference, units, weights, process/material assumptions, and the maximum
   number of variants. Use 3–8 variants unless the user supplied another
   bounded set.
3. **Confirm real parameters.** Use `set_param`, `evaluate_script`, and
   `diff_scripts` or `diff_geometry` to prove that each proposed parameter
   changes the intended geometry. A parameter that does not affect the model is
   not a design variable.
4. **Generate comparable candidates.** Change only declared variables. Keep
   interfaces, units, material basis, load cases, DFM process, and acceptance
   requirements constant. Give every candidate an ID and exact source digest.
5. **Evaluate every candidate.** Run full `evaluate_script`; inspect the same
   metrics for all candidates; run the same `dfm_review`; and, where the inputs
   are complete, the same `sweep_tolerance` and `run_fea` studies.
6. **Reject ineligible candidates first.** A hard-constraint failure, missing
   mandatory metric, `NOT_RUN` mandatory check, or `UNSUPPORTED` mandatory check
   makes a candidate ineligible. Do not rescue it with a high weighted score.
7. **Compute the score.** Normalize and calculate scores from returned values as
   specified in `references/scoring-and-sensitivity.md`. Do not rank by eye.
8. **Run sensitivity.** Perturb each nonzero weight by −20% and +20%,
   renormalize, and report winner flips. Also report the single criterion that
   contributes most to the selected candidate’s lead.
9. **Explain both sides.** For each candidate, list supporting evidence,
   contradicting evidence, and the smallest additional test that would resolve
   its largest uncertainty.
10. **Prepare, do not silently select.** Present the ranked matrix and
    recommendation. Save or open the selected variant only after the user
    approves it. Never overwrite the baseline.

## Required output

1. **Recommendation and confidence.**
2. **Baseline identity.**
3. **Decision criteria:** units, directions, hard constraints, weights.
4. **Candidate matrix:** exact revision/digest, eligibility, raw values,
   normalized values, score, and evidence states.
5. **For / against / uncertainty** for every candidate.
6. **Sensitivity:** weight perturbations, winner flips, dominant criterion.
7. **Cheapest discriminating test:** one test that resolves the most important
   remaining uncertainty for the least work.
8. **Approval gate:** the candidate is recommended, not committed.

Never call the highest-scoring variant “optimal” outside the tested candidate
set and assumptions.

skills.name: kernelcad-cookbooks
skills.desc: Find and run kernelCAD cookbook recipes (machined housing, NEMA motor plate, robot arm, planetary gearbox, T-slot frame, enclosures) through the hosted MCP. Use before freehand authoring of an industry part.
skills.body:
---
name: kernelcad-cookbooks
description: Find and run kernelCAD cookbook recipes (machined housing, NEMA motor plate, robot arm, planetary gearbox, T-slot frame, enclosures) through the hosted MCP. Use before freehand authoring of an industry part.
---

# kernelCAD cookbooks

1. `lookup_cookbook({ query: "<what the user wants>", k: 5 })` returns ranked
   recipes `{ ok, hits[] }`. Empty `hits` is a valid answer: author freehand.
2. Run a hit in one step: `execute_cookbook({ id, openInStudio: false })`.
   Read `stage` on failure (`resolve` | `evaluate` | `open_in_studio`).
   `dryRun: true` is not proof that the recipe builds a solid.
3. Adapt the returned `code` to the user's dimensions, then go through the
   `kernelcad-design-loop` skill.

Useful ids: `multi-feature-machined-housing`, `nema-motor-mounting-plate`,
`multi-body-mechanism-real-proportions`, `multi-dof-robot-arm-4axis`,
`planetary-gearbox-shop-release`, `gt2-shop-release-actuator`,
`clamshell-enclosure-release-pack`, `tslot-frame-fastener-bom`,
`scissor-lift-closed-loop`, `holeless-board-cradle` (no-hole development board rail and connector opening).

skills.name: kernelcad-design-loop
skills.desc: Build or revise a CAD model with the hosted kernelCAD MCP — write .kcad.ts source, evaluate, review with design_loop until green. Use for any "design / model / make a part" request when the kernelcad MCP server is connected.
skills.body:
---
name: kernelcad-design-loop
description: Build or revise a CAD model with the hosted kernelCAD MCP — write .kcad.ts source, evaluate, review with design_loop until green. Use for any "design / model / make a part" request when the kernelcad MCP server is connected.
---

# kernelCAD design loop (hosted MCP)

The `kernelcad` MCP server (https://mcp.kernelcad.com/mcp) runs the OpenCASCADE
kernel for you. Nothing needs to be installed locally. Discover the live tool
list from the server; tool availability depends on whether the user is signed in.

## Loop

1. Check for a canonical pattern first: `lookup_cookbook({ query })`
   (see the `kernelcad-cookbooks` skill). Start from a hit when one exists.
2. Write `.kcad.ts` source. Use `lookup_api({})` for the API surface instead of guessing.
3. Iterate fast with `evaluate_script({ code, dryRun: true })`, then finish with a
   full `evaluate_script({ code })`. A dry run is not evidence that the solid builds.
4. For housings, mechanisms, gearboxes, robot arms and other production builds,
   call `design_loop({ goal, attempts: [{ code }] })`. Apply its
   `nextActionPrompt` / `revisionAssist` patches and repeat until `ok: true`
   or `convergence.escalate` says to stop and ask the user.
5. On failure, `why_did_this_fail({ code })` then `repair_script({ code })`.
   `lookup_diagnostics({})` explains any diagnostic code.
6. For assemblies that must be built, run
   `verify({ check: 'assembly-path', sequence: true })`. Declare helical
   fastener motion and press/snap fits on the fastened mate
   (`{ fastener: { part?, axis, pitchMm?, tool? }, fit?: { kind, part? } }`);
   the planner reports `helical`, `requires-force` and `tool-blocked` steps
   instead of guessing. Add `stability: true` (with `gravity`/`fixtures` when
   needed) to flag steps whose part cannot be proven to rest on an
   already-stable part: read `sequence.needsHold` and `Step.heldBy`. That is an
   approximate support projection, not physics. Tool reach is a swept
   envelope, not a hardware check.
7. Show the result once with `open_in_studio` (see `kernelcad-studio-paint`),
   then export (see `kernelcad-export`).

## Rules

- Report the numbers the tools return (volumes, bbox, diagnostics); do not
  describe geometry you have not evaluated.
- Keep the source as the deliverable: give the user the final `.kcad.ts`.
- If a tool says sign-in is required, tell the user to complete the OAuth
  prompt their client shows for the `kernelcad` server.

skills.name: kernelcad-export
skills.desc: Export a kernelCAD model to STEP, STL, 3MF, GLB, OBJ, PLY, USD, DXF or G-code through the hosted MCP, and check it before handing it over. Use when the user asks for a file to print, machine, simulate or import into other CAD.
skills.body:
---
name: kernelcad-export
description: Export a kernelCAD model to STEP, STL, 3MF, GLB, OBJ, PLY, USD, DXF or G-code through the hosted MCP, and check it before handing it over. Use when the user asks for a file to print, machine, simulate or import into other CAD.
---

# Export

- Whole model: `export({ target: "model", code, format, output_path })` with
  `format` one of `step`, `stl`, `3mf`, `glb`, `obj`, `ply`, `usd`, `dxf`, `gcode`.
  `obj` is a Wavefront triangle mesh. `ply` is a Stanford PLY triangle mesh
  (mm, Z-up; binary little-endian by default) with per-vertex normals and
  the part colour from `.finish()` / `.material()` / `.color()`; an assembly is
  one file with every part in world space. Options: `encoding: 'ascii'`,
  `colors: 'face'` or `'none'`, `normals: false`; a bad key fails with
  `export.ply.invalid-options`. `usd` is an ASCII USDA triangle mesh
  with millimeter units and Z-up coordinates; it is not B-rep USD. NVIDIA's
  usd-brep BrepArray is not emitted because this writer consumes tessellated
  vertices and triangle indices, while BrepArray requires full B-rep topology
  and curve/surface data. Use `usd-isaac` separately for an assembly physics
  stage. Options: `3mf` takes `printUnit` and `embedSource`; `dxf` takes `unit`,
  `tolerance`, `layers`; `glb` takes `axis`.
- Per part of an assembly: `export({ target: "part", code, output_dir })`.
- Before exporting for print: `inspect({ of: "part-stats", code })`. For a
  bill of materials: `inspect({ of: "bom", code })`.
- Verify a STEP after export with `inspect({ of: "step", file })`.
- Before handing an assembly to a physics simulator, call `check_export_health`
  with the same `file` or `code`. It compiles the MJCF and runs forward at
  `qpos0`, the authored mate pose (scalar joint `ref`: degrees to radians,
  millimetres to metres; the child body frame is that pose, and joint
  coordinate 0 stays the connector-aligned pose; a ball joint has no `ref`
  because its `qpos0` stays the identity quaternion, and the authored XYZ
  Euler triple is the child body quaternion; a coupled driven joint follows
  `ratio × source + offset`). It reports unexpected rest contacts, visual
  geoms that still collide, mass / centre of mass / inertia against the CAD
  solid for both the MJCF body and the URDF inertial, and any `qpos0` outside
  its joint range. A contact is a collision-geometry artefact
  (`collisionGeomArtefact`, with `cadExactOverlapMm3` and `cadDistanceMm`)
  only when the exact CAD overlap is at or below 0.01 mm³ and the CAD
  clearance is finite and greater than 0.01 mm. That artefact does not fail
  the check. Zero, missing, or smaller clearance stays a real contact. A
  declared `massKg` is the mass on both exports. When mass properties throw,
  both exports substitute unit inertia and the row is a fallback. It does not replace
  `verify({ check: "physics" })`, which still starts unnamed sample mates at
  coordinate 0. The local evidence bundle is
  `docs/demos/export-health-authored-rest-20261117/README.md`.
- The hosted server returns a download link or file reference; give the user
  that link and say which format and units it is in. Keep verification on
  (do not pass `no_verify: true`) unless the user asks.

skills.name: kernelcad-studio-paint
skills.desc: Show a kernelCAD model in Studio and act on the user's painted review marks. Use when the user wants to see the model, or says they marked/painted/circled something in Studio.
skills.body:
---
name: kernelcad-studio-paint
description: Show a kernelCAD model in Studio and act on the user's painted review marks. Use when the user wants to see the model, or says they marked/painted/circled something in Studio.
---

# Studio viewer and paint review

## Save and show the model

After a successful full `evaluate_script`, call `open_in_studio` with the
final `code`. Evaluation alone does not confirm that a project was saved.
For an existing design, also pass `project` with the exact returned slug;
do not create a replacement project for a revision.

Handle the returned state before claiming completion:

- `status: "running"` or code `tool.still-running`: the save has not completed.
  Call `open_in_studio` again with the same arguments to join the running save.
  Do not set `new_project: true`, alter the source, or claim a saved revision
  while joining it. If it remains pending within the available execution
  budget, report that state rather than inventing a result.
- A completed save with `meshStatus: "building"`: reuse its returned slug,
  revision and URL, and poll `get_project({ slug })` for mesh readiness.
  Do not repeat `open_in_studio` to poll a saved project's mesh.
- A successful completed result: reuse the returned URL, revision and preview.
  Show one successful viewer per project per response; do not call
  `open_in_studio` again after success in that response.
- `ok: false` or `meshStatus: "failed"`: report the returned failure and repair
  the specific problem before retrying. Do not describe a failed save or mesh
  as an available model.

Report `projectSaved`, `meshReady` and `previewDelivered` only when the response
establishes those states. `viewerPainted` requires an actual widget
acknowledgement; a returned URL does not prove that the user's client rendered
it. On clients without the interactive widget, provide the returned web URL
and supported download links instead of claiming an in-chat viewer appeared.

For a later revision, retrieve the existing source with `get_project({ slug })`,
evaluate the changes, then call `open_in_studio({ project: slug, code })`.
Keep the exact project identity and return the new revision when it is saved.

## Paint review

In Studio the user can paint over the model to mark what to change. Fetch the
newest marks for that model with `review_paint_peek_latest({ slug })` using its
exact project slug (pass `paths_only: true` to skip inline PNGs). Do not fetch
unscoped latest feedback when the target project is known. The packet holds a
screenshot, a red mask and the list of parts the paint hit. Edit only those
parts, re-evaluate, and save the revision to the same project.
If the tool returns `empty`, ask the user to paint and submit again. This tool
is only available when the server can access the relevant feedback; if absent,
ask the user to describe the change in words.

skills.name: manufacturing-readiness
skills.desc: Review one exact kernelCAD revision for fabrication readiness. Use when the user asks whether a part or assembly is ready to print, machine, fabricate, quote, or release. Produces revision-bound evidence with PASS, FAIL, WARN, NOT_RUN, UNSUPPORTED, and ASSUMPTION states; it never converts missing checks into a pass and never sends a quote or order without explicit approval.
skills.body:
---
name: manufacturing-readiness
description: >-
  Review one exact kernelCAD revision for fabrication readiness. Use when the user asks whether a part or assembly is ready to print, machine, fabricate, quote, or release. Produces revision-bound evidence with PASS, FAIL, WARN, NOT_RUN, UNSUPPORTED, and ASSUMPTION states; it never converts missing checks into a pass and never sends a quote or order without explicit approval.
---

# Manufacturing readiness

A useful readiness report answers one narrow question:

> What is supported for this exact design revision, for these named processes,
> and what still blocks a manufacturing handoff?

It is not a visual opinion and it is not a supplier approval.

Read `references/evidence-contract.md` before running the workflow.

## Workflow

1. **Freeze the subject.** Prefer a saved project and call `get_project_revision`
   with the exact `slug` and `version`. Otherwise use the exact inline `.kcad.ts`
   source. Record the project slug/version or a SHA-256 of the source. Never mix
   results from two revisions.
2. **Read the request.** Record the requested process, material, quantity,
   tolerance targets, load cases, machine envelope, and any supplier-specific
   limits. Missing inputs stay missing. Do not infer them from appearance.
3. **Build the geometry.** Run a full `evaluate_script`. A dry run is not
   evidence that the solid builds. Record `buildOk`, `ok`, bounding box,
   volume, diagnostics, requirement results, and tool limitations.
4. **Inspect the model.** Use `inspect` for the facts needed by the request:
   part statistics, body/part count, BOM, holes, wall/section metrics, or STEP
   verification. Do not run unrelated readers merely to make the report longer.
5. **Review assemblies only when present.** Use `review_cad` or `design_loop`
   for mechanisms and multi-part products. Record skipped stages separately.

---
name: kernelcad-authoring
description: kernelCAD model authoring API — primitives, transforms, booleans, sketches, path-builder, sketch-text, return-single-shape rule, conventions, CLI commands, and verification gates. Load this when writing or modifying .kcad.ts geometry.
---

# kernelCAD — authoring

Write or edit `.kcad.ts` TypeScript models; run `kernelcad evaluate <file>` or `kernelcad export stl|step|dxf|3mf|glb <file> -o <out>`.

Single-file scripts refuse top-level `import`/`require` with `feature.invalid-args`; define helpers in the same file.

Core: units, failure prevention, API selection and finish checks. Full signatures, CLI flags, materials and recipes are in `references/*.md`; use `lookup_authoring_skill({ section: '<id>' })` or `{ query: '...' }` over MCP (index below).

## Coordinate System

- **Z-up**, right-handed. Lengths in millimetres, angles in degrees.
- `box(x, y, z)`: corner-anchored at the origin (spans `[0, x] × [0, y] × [0, z]`). `box(x, y, z, true)` centres ALL three axes.
- `cylinder(h, r)`: axis along Z, centred in X/Y, base at `z = 0`, top at `z = h` (no centred flag).
- `sphere(r)`: centred on the origin.
- `path()...close()` builds a Sketch in XY; `.extrude(d)` goes +Z; `.revolve()` turns the (radial X, axial Z) profile about Z.
- **Return rule**: the script `return`s ONE `Shape`, or one assembly via `assembly(...).model()` / `.solvedModel()`. Only the returned value is exported, probed and measured. A script with no `return` still evaluates on the last CREATED shape (often a cutter or helper) and gets the warning `script.no-return` — treat it as a bug and add the `return`.

## Conventions

The rules that prevent most failed evaluations (from the diagnostics catalogue and repair telemetry). Fix the cause, not the symptom.

1. **Params work in plain JS math.** `w + 4`, `Math.sin(a)` use the current value; an edit re-runs only what changed. `.add/.multiply/.clamp` keep it symbolic. Declare params at the top with units; every numeric argument must be finite (`NaN`/`undefined` fails capture).
2. **Holes are features, not cylinders.** Use `hole` / `holes` / `cutout` instead of `subtract(cylinder(...))`: they drill the right size (threads, counterbores, countersinks), name their faces (`'wall'`, `'floor'`, `'counterbore-*'`, `'countersink-cone'`) and reach drawings, BOM and DFM. Hole `u`/`v` are mm offsets from the CENTRE of the entry face (`top`/`bottom`: u=+X, v=+Y; `front`/`back`: u=+X, v=+Z; `left`/`right`: u=+Y, v=+Z), not world coordinates.
3. **Booleans need real overlap.** Give unions ≥ 0.1 mm of overlap and cut tools ≥ 0.1 mm of run-out past the faces; never rely on coincident or tangent faces. A cut that misses the body is `feature.subtractive-noop` — check the tool's position and axis.
4. **One union, one connected body.** `union.disconnected` = an operand floats; move it to touch. `union.member-overlap` = same-stock pieces overlap; fuse first and `.finish()` once, or butt them (`span - 2 * railWidth`). Each member keeps its own finish: no part per colour.
5. **Separate components are named parts.** Every physically distinct component is `assembly().part(name, shape)`; parts that touch or move get connectors and a mate (`'fastened'`, `'revolute'`, `'prismatic'`, `'cylindrical'`, `'planar'`, ...) with limits — not raw `translate()` offsets. Loose top-level bodies emit `assembly.structure.unstructured-bodies`.
6. **Sketches are one closed loop.** Close the path, drop zero-length segments and duplicate points; a revolve profile stays at `x ≥ 0` (`feature.revolve.crosses-axis`).
7. **Fillets and chamfers fit the wall.** Keep the radius below half the local wall thickness, and every target edge at least 2 × radius long (`feature.edge-feature.short-edges-skipped`) — round a plate's corners in its outline (`extrudeRoundedRect`) rather than filleting short vertical edges (`repair-oversized-fillet`); fillet/chamfer/shell BEFORE the boolean that splits the face (`feature.face-ref.ambiguous-after-split`) and before transforms when you address faces by name.
8. **Face names exist only where a primitive defines them.** Box: all six (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `front`, `back`); cylinder: `top`/`bottom` only; sphere, extruded sketches, `extrudeRoundedRect`, revolves and lofts: none (`feature.face-ref.not-applicable`). Pick those faces, and faces a cavity cut duplicated, by query: `{ byNormal: 'Z' }`, `{ byNormal: '-Z', atZ: 0 }`, `{ byNormal: 'Z', extreme: 'Z' }`.
9. **Await async helpers.** `selectEdges`, `lib.fromSTEP`, `lib.fromNativeCAD`, `lib.from3MF`, `lib.fetchPart`, `.boundingBox()`, `.recenter()` and `.seatOnFloor()` return promises (`feature.async-result.missing-await`).
10. **Read the diagnostic, then repair one cause.** Every diagnostic carries a `hint`; follow it. `recompute.input.missing` means an upstream feature failed — call `why_did_this_fail`. Never export or hand over a script whose last evaluate failed.
11. **Do not declare something impossible** without calling `lookup_api` and `lookup_cookbook` first. `lookup_api({ query: 'arcTo' })` maps other tools' names (`references/idioms.md`). kernelCAD does NURBS lofts, sweeps, boundary patches and G2 blends; it is not a polygon sculptor or a photoreal renderer.
12. **Helical geometry**: rail from `helix(...)`, sweep with `spine: 'helix'` (threads, worms) or `spine: 'smooth'` (wire springs). Internal threads are `hole({ thread })`, never a sweep. `.mirror(plane)` = source + reflection; `.reflect(plane)` = reflection only.

## Manufacturing intent → API

Intent words → call this API; do not hand-build it (subtracted cylinders, typed involute or polygon points, unioned plates). Recipe: `lookup_cookbook(<id>)`.

| Intent words | API | Cookbook id |
|---|---|---|
| bolt hole, clearance hole, M3–M8 | `body.holes(face, { positions: [{ u, v }], diameter, depth: 'through' })`; ISO 273 clearance M3 3.4 · M4 4.5 · M5 5.5 · M6 6.6 · M8 9 | clearance-hole-through-plate |
| thread, tapped, tap drill, M-size into the part | `body.threadedHole(face, { u, v, spec: 'M5', depth })` (`modeled: true` = real thread) or `body.hole(face, { diameter: <nominal>, depth, thread: true })` (12 → M12×1.75); an explicit `thread: { pitch }` still works; coarse P: M3 0.5 · M4 0.7 · M5 0.8 · M6 1 · M8 1.25 | threaded-hole-tap-drill |
| external thread, threaded rod, bolt, jar neck | `threadedRod({ spec: 'M6', length })` (+ union a head); `isoThread(spec)` gives pitch / tap drill | iso-metric-bolt-and-nut |
| counterbore, socket head flush | `body.hole(face, { diameter, depth, counterbore: { diameter, depth } })` (M3 Ø6.5×3.4, M4 Ø8×4.4, M5 Ø10×5.4, M6 Ø11×6.4) | drawing-hole-and-gdt-callouts |
| countersink, flat head flush | `body.hole(face, { diameter, depth, countersink: { diameter, angleDeg: 90 } })` | countersunk-flat-head-screw |
| bent tube, pipe, hydraulic / fuel / coolant line between fittings, bend table | `tube(name, opts)` + `tubeSpec(rules)` between `part.port(name)`s (skill `kernelcad-tubes`) | pipe-route-swept-tube |
| heat-set insert | blind `hole` at the insert pilot Ø | heat-set-insert-pilot |
| nut trap, captive nut | `hole` + `cutout(hexPath, { face, depth })` | hex-nut-trap-bolt-clearance |
| set screw, radial hole, cross hole | `hole({ ofSurfaceType: 'CYLINDER' }, { at: { angleDeg, z }, diameter, depth: 'through', thread })` straight into the round side (`'through'` stops at the bore; `at: [x, y, z]` + optional `axis` for any face / angle); a spot-face flat first is optional | threaded-hole-tap-drill |
| hole pattern, bolt circle, grid of holes | one `body.holes(face, { positions })` with computed positions; `patternLinear` / `patternGrid` / `patternCircular` for repeated bodies | clearance-hole-through-plate |
| slot, D-cut, keyhole, irregular opening | `cutout(path().slot(0, 0, { width, centerDistance }), { face, depth })`, profile measured from the face centre | hex-nut-trap-bolt-clearance |
| pocket, recess | blind `cutout` or blind `hole` (`depth: n`) | blind-pocket-from-top |
| enclosure, box, case, hollow, wall thickness | `.shell(wall, { face: 'top' })` on the outer body, or subtract the inner box; lid = second part | enclosure-lid-with-screw-bosses |
| standoffs, bosses, PCB / Raspberry Pi mount | union `cylinder` bosses on the floor, then `holes(..., { thread })` or insert pilots through them | enclosure-lid-with-screw-bosses |
| gear, involute, module, pinion | `spurGear({ module, teeth, faceWidth, bore, backlash })`, `spurGearPair`, `ringGear`; centre distance m(z1+z2)/2 | involute-spur-gear-pair |
| sheet metal, bend, flange, flat pattern | `sheetMetal(profile, { thickness, kFactor }).bend({ atX }, angle, radius)` — lines in blank coordinates, the shorter side folds, chain bends for U / Z; drill the blank before bending; MCP `flatten_pattern` | sheet-metal-l-bracket-bend |
| fit, clearance, tolerance, printer | clearance param (per side: press 0.05 · snap 0.15 · slip 0.2 · running 0.3) + `dfmSpec({ process: 'fdm', printer, minClearance })` | fdm-fit-clearance-by-fit-type |
| hinge, pivot, rotating joint | two `assembly().part`s, axis `connector`s, `mate(name, a, b, 'revolute', { limitsDeg })` | clamshell-hinge-two-part-assembly |
| shaft in bearing, slider | `'cylindrical'` / `'prismatic'` mate between connectors | shaft-and-bearing-cylindrical-mate |
| rounded edges, chamfered edges | `.fillet(r, selector)` / `.chamfer(d, selector)` after the booleans that make the edges | fillet-face-after-subtract |
| knob, pulley, turned part | `path()` half-profile `.revolve()` | revolve-rectangular-profile |
| L-bracket from plates | plates that touch without overlap, one union | non-overlapping-l-bracket |
| motor mount, NEMA 17 | `holes` on the 31 mm pattern + pilot bore | nema-motor-mounting-plate |
| photo, trace, reference image | MCP `trace_from_image` (`referenceImage` only overlays) | resolve-photo-trace-assumptions |
| infill, weak spots, stronger, will it hold, stress | `feaStudy` + `export` 3mf `infill: { fromFea }` (local ccx + gmsh) | stress-graded-infill-fdm |
| screw, nut, bearing, motor, servo | `lib.standard.*`, `lib.findPart`, MCP `find_part` | kernelcad-parts |

## Before you finish

A clean evaluate proves the script ran, not that it is the part the user asked for. A solid block is valid geometry and still fails the design. Before you report done:

1. **Re-read the request and list every must-have** — each hole, opening, cavity, wall, rib, part, clearance and joint — and point to the source line that builds it. Anything without a line is missing.
2. **Measure, do not trust your summary.** `inspect({ of: 'shape' })` (bbox, volume) must match the stated outer dimensions; hollow volume is far below bbox volume.
3. **Holes**: count, diameter, position, through vs blind as asked; threads made with `thread`, counterbores and countersinks with their options.
4. **Walls**: hollow parts are hollow with the stated wall (`inspect({ of: 'section' })` or a section render); printed parts declare `dfmSpec({ minWall })`.
5. **Parts and motion**: separate components are separate named parts; joints carry mates with limits; `kernelcad interference` is clean and nothing floats.
6. **Manufacturing method**: printed → clearances + `dfmSpec`; sheet metal → `sheetMetal()` + flat pattern; bought parts → catalog or STEP, or labelled placeholders.
7. **Look**: render top, front and iso (`render_preview` / `kernelcad render`) and check that openings, text and holes are where the request put them.
8. **Deliver**: the last `evaluate` is clean and the requested exports (STEP, STL, 3MF) were produced from it.

## Workflow

1. **Classify** the job (blockout, production part, reference replication, assembly/mechanism, sheet metal, standard-part integration) and load the matching skill.
2. **Brief**: purpose, outer dimensions, interfaces, moving parts, manufacturing method. If load-bearing dimensions are missing, ask 1–3 questions or encode each as a named `param()`.
3. **Route** each feature through the table above; `lookup_cookbook` the recipe.
4. **Write** the `.kcad.ts`, evaluate, repair one diagnostic at a time.
5. **Verify** with measurements and renders, then run **Before you finish**.
6. **Prebuilt art** (games, three.js): browse the shipped low-poly kits with `search_assets`, `get_asset`, `find_matching`, `get_variant`, `list_kits`, `get_kit` instead of modelling from scratch.

Full loop and artifact policy: `agent-authoring-loop` (`references/workflow.md`).

<!-- OUT-OF-SCOPE:START -->
## Out of Scope

These are not available today; do not generate code that uses them. Anything not listed here is fair game — call `lookup_api` / `lookup_cookbook` before concluding kernelCAD lacks a capability.

- Asymmetric chamfer (only symmetric 45° supported) — deferred
- Param-bound (auto-updating) dimensions on `svg-drawing` — deferred; dimensions DO ship derived from the geometry (`options.autoAnnotate`: datums, hole callouts with position tolerances, positions, radii, chamfers, flatness, ISO 2768 note), authored (`options.annotations`), and as section views on any plane (`options.sections`)
- NURBS surface extend/untrim/blend/quilt — deferred (surface-surface intersection ships as `surfaceIntersection`)
- Tracked face/edge refs (only canonical refs and inline queries work) — deferred

<!-- OUT-OF-SCOPE:END -->

## Reference index

Read the file, or pull a section id with `lookup_authoring_skill({ section: '<id>' })`.

| File | Section ids | Read it when |
|---|---|---|
| `references/workflow.md` | `agent-authoring-loop`, `inner-loop-render-after-every-visible-change`, `assembly-and-mechanism-loop`, `source-and-artifact-policy`, `standard-parts-and-vendor-geometry`, `installation` | multi-part or mechanism work, renders, vendor STEP |
| `references/api.md` | `api-surface` (`top-level-functions`, `selector-algebra-shapelist`, `shape-methods-chainable`, `sketch-methods`, `pathbuilder-methods`, `2d-text-sketch-text`, `constrained-sketches-v0-4-mcp`), `labels-naming-faces-at-creation-time` | you need an exact signature |
| `references/verification.md` | `when-something-fails`, `verification-gates`, `dfm-gates-print-readiness` | a diagnostic you do not understand; print gates |
| `references/cli.md` | `cli-commands`, `animation-timelines-animationview` | CLI flags, renders, animation capture |
| `references/recipes.md` | `interlocking-joinery-flat-pack-laser-cnc`, `hardware-belts-and-wood-joinery`, `sample` | joinery, belts, worked examples |
| `references/materials.md` | `materials`, `reference-images` | finishes, colours, PBR, image overlays |
| `references/cookbook-index.md` | `cookbook-snippet-index` | every cookbook id and its trigger |

## Related skills

- `kernelcad-features` — load when adding fillets, chamfers, shells, holes, or cutouts.
- `kernelcad-params` — load when the model needs editable `param()` / `params()` values or live slider support.
- `kernelcad-assemblies` — load for multi-part models with joints, mates, or connectors.
- `kernelcad-sheet-metal` — load for bent parts and flat patterns.
- `kernelcad-nurbs` — load for freeform NURBS surfaces that primitives and sketches cannot express.
- `kernelcad-from-reference` — load when building from a reference photo or visual brief; extends the verification gate set.
- `kernelcad-mcp` — load instead of this skill when you need to introspect a running model dynamically via MCP tools.

| thread, tapped, tap drill, M-size into the part | `body.threadedHole(face, { u, v, spec: 'M5', depth })` (`modeled: true` = real thread) or `body.hole(face, { diameter: <nominal>, depth, thread: true })` (12 → M12×1.75); an explicit `thread: { pitch }` still works; coarse P: M3 0.5 · M4 0.7 · M5 0.8 · M6 1 · M8 1.25 | threaded-hole-tap-drill |
| external thread, threaded rod, bolt, jar neck | `threadedRod({ spec: 'M6', length })` (+ union a head); `isoThread(spec)` gives pitch / tap drill | iso-metric-bolt-and-nut |

## Before you finish

A clean evaluate proves the script ran, not that it is the part the user asked for. A solid block is valid geometry and still fails the design. Before you report done:

1. **Re-read the request and list every must-have** — each hole, opening, cavity, wall, rib, part, clearance and joint — and point to the source line that builds it. Anything without a line is missing.
2. **Measure, do not trust your summary.** `inspect({ of: 'shape' })` (bbox, volume) must match the stated outer dimensions; hollow volume is far below bbox volume.
3. **Holes**: count, diameter, position, through vs blind as asked; threads made with `thread`, counterbores and countersinks with their options.
4. **Walls**: hollow parts are hollow with the stated wall (`inspect({ of: 'section' })` or a section render); printed parts declare `dfmSpec({ minWall })`.
5. **Parts and motion**: separate components are separate named parts; joints carry mates with limits; `kernelcad interference` is clean and nothing floats.
6. **Manufacturing method**: printed → clearances + `dfmSpec`; sheet metal → `sheetMetal()` + flat pattern; bought parts → catalog or STEP, or labelled placeholders.
7. **Look**: render top, front and iso (`render_preview` / `kernelcad render`) and check that openings, text and holes are where the request put them.
8. **Deliver**: the last `evaluate` is clean and the requested exports (STEP, STL, 3MF) were produced from it.

## Workflow

1. **Classify** the job (blockout, production part, reference replication, assembly/mechanism, sheet metal, standard-part integration) and load the matching skill.
2. **Brief**: purpose, outer dimensions, interfaces, moving parts, manufacturing method. If load-bearing dimensions are missing, ask 1–3 questions or encode each as a named `param()`.
3. **Route** each feature through the table above; `lookup_cookbook` the recipe.
4. **Write** the `.kcad.ts`, evaluate, repair one diagnostic at a time.
5. **Verify** with measurements and renders, then run **Before you finish**.
6. **Prebuilt art** (games, three.js): browse the shipped low-poly kits with `search_assets`, `get_asset`, `find_matching`, `get_variant`, `list_kits`, `get_kit` instead of modelling from scratch.

Full loop and artifact policy: `agent-authoring-loop` (`references/workflow.md`).

<!-- OUT-OF-SCOPE:START -->
## Out of Scope

These are not available today; do not generate code that uses them. Anything not listed here is fair game — call `lookup_api` / `lookup_cookbook` before concluding kernelCAD lacks a capability.

- Asymmetric chamfer (only symmetric 45° supported) — deferred
- Param-bound (auto-updating) dimensions on `svg-drawing` — deferred; dimensions DO ship derived from the geometry (`options.autoAnnotate`: datums, hole callouts with position tolerances, positions, radii, chamfers, flatness, ISO 2768 note), authored (`options.annotations`), and as section views on any plane (`options.sections`)
- NURBS surface extend/untrim/blend/quilt — deferred (surface-surface intersection ships as `surfaceIntersection`)
- Tracked face/edge refs (only canonical refs and inline queries work) — deferred

<!-- OUT-OF-SCOPE:END -->

skills.desc: Answer "how much pressure does this duct, pipe or manifold cost, how does the flow split, and how much drag does this part see?" with OpenFOAM evidence — declare a steady incompressible flow study with shape.cfdStudy({ flow, fluid, inlet, outlet, velocity | flowRateLpm }) or pass it on the call, then run it with run_cfd (or `kernelcad cfd run`) for pressure drop, per-outlet flow and mass balance, drag / lift with Cd / Cl, max velocity, the Reynolds number and turbulence model, a residual history with a convergence verdict, checkMesh quality and a mid-plane velocity PNG. skills.body:
---
name: kernelcad-cfd
description: Answer "how much pressure does this duct, pipe or manifold cost, how does the flow split, and how much drag does this part see?" with OpenFOAM evidence — declare a steady incompressible flow study with shape.cfdStudy({ flow, fluid, inlet, outlet, velocity | flowRateLpm }) or pass it on the call, then run it with run_cfd (or `kernelcad cfd run`) for pressure drop, per-outlet flow and mass balance, drag / lift with Cd / Cl, max velocity, the Reynolds number and turbulence model, a residual history with a convergence verdict, checkMesh quality and a mid-plane velocity PNG. Use when sizing a coolant manifold, air duct, nozzle or pipe run, or when a part sits in a stream.
---

# kernelCAD — CFD (OpenFOAM)

Declare the flow in the model, run the solver, read the evidence.

```typescript
const manifold = box(60, 40, 16)
  .hole('left', { u: 0, v: 0, diameter: 8, depth: 40 })
  .hole('right', { u: -10, v: 0, diameter: 5, depth: 26 })
  .hole('right', { u: 10, v: 0, diameter: 4, depth: 26 })
  .subtract(cylinder(24, 3).rotate([1, 0, 0], -90).translate(37, 8, 8));   // printed gallery

manifold.cfdStudy({
  name: 'splitter',
  flow: 'internal',
  fluid: 'water',
  inlet: { atX: 0 },                                                // the 8 mm port opening
  outlet: [{ atX: 60, near: [60, 10, 8] }, { atX: 60, near: [60, 30, 8] }],
  flowRateLpm: 0.3,
});
return manifold;
```

```
run_cfd({ file: 'manifold.kcad.ts', output_dir: '/tmp/manifold-cfd' })
// → { ok: true, summary: { pressureDropPa: 48.7, reynolds: { value: 794 }, turbulence: { model: 'laminar' },
//     patches: [inlet -0.3 L/min, outlet_1 0.179 L/min, outlet_2 0.121 L/min], massBalance: { imbalance: 9e-5 },
//     convergence: { verdict: 'converged', criterion: 'monitors', ... }, mesh: { cells: 17504, ok: true } },
//     images: ['/tmp/manifold-cfd/velocity-midplane.png'] }
```

The same study on the call, without a declaration:
`run_cfd({ code, flow: 'external', fluid: 'air', velocity: 10, direction: '+X' })`.
From the shell: `kernelcad cfd run part.kcad.ts [--flow ... --inlet '{"atX":0}' ...]`;
`kernelcad cfd status` (= `cfd_summary`) says whether OpenFOAM is installed.

## The fluid domain

- **Internal, `fluidVolume: 'interior'` (default).** The fluid is the part's
  channels: the bounding box minus the part, keeping the regions an inlet or
  outlet opens into. Channels must open **flush onto the part's bounding box**
  (pipe ends, manifold ports on the outer faces); a port recessed behind a boss
  leaks into the exterior and fails with `cfd.domain.no-fluid`. Bolt holes are
  enclosed voids no inlet reaches, so they are dropped.
- **Internal, `fluidVolume: 'solid'`.** The solid itself is the fluid (model
  the flow passage directly).
- **External.** A box of fluid around the part (3 body lengths up and to the
  sides, 8 downstream), `velocity` along `direction`; the body is one wall
  patch `body`, the box faces are `inlet`, `outlet` and slip `sides`.

`inlet` / `outlet` are FaceQuery selectors (or refs) **on the fluid volume**:
`{ atX: 0 }` is the opening disc, not the part's end face. Several faces at the
same plane: use `near: [x, y, z]` to pick one. An `outlet` array makes
`outlet_1`, `outlet_2`, ... and reports the split. A selector that matches no
fluid face fails with `cfd.study.patch-unresolved` listing the fluid faces.

## Study fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `flow` | `'internal'` or `'external'` (required). |
| `fluid` | `'water'` (998.2 kg/m³, 1.004e-6 m²/s), `'air'` (1.205, 1.511e-5), or `{ rho, nu }` SI. |
| `velocity` | m/s: normal inlet speed (internal) or free stream (external). |
| `flowRateLpm` | internal alternative to `velocity`, L/min. |
| `outletPressurePa` | gauge, default 0. |
| `meshSize` | surface cell mm, or `'coarse'` (8 cells across the inlet / body), `'medium'` (14, default), `'fine'` (22). |
| `iterations` | SIMPLE cap, default 400 (10..5000). |
| `residualTarget` | default 1e-4. |
| `turbulence` | `'auto'` (default): laminar below Re 2300 internal / 1000 external, k-omega SST above (2300..4000 flagged transitional). |
| `referenceAreaMm2` | external Cd / Cl area; default projected frontal area. |

## Reading the result

- `ok` is **true only when the solve converged**. `convergence.criterion` says
  how: `'residuals'` (target met) or `'monitors'` (residuals plateaued below
  5e-2 but the pressure drop / drag stayed within a 1% band over the last 20%
  of iterations, mass balanced to 0.5%, at least 200 iterations).
- Not converged: `ok: false`, `cfd.solve.not-converged`, and
  `convergence.monitor { mean, band }` — the honest error bar. Flows with
  impinging jets at Re above ~1000 are often physically unsteady; a steady
  solve will not settle. Lower the flow, smooth the junction, or treat the
  mean ± band as the answer.
- `cfd.flow.regime-caveat` (info): transitional pipe flow, a shedding wake, or
  steady RANS drag — read the number as an estimate.
- `mesh.ok` false → `cfd.mesh.quality-low`; `cfd.mesh.failed` when snappy
  found nothing to mesh or the fluid leaked into the background box.
- Every summary carries `disclaimer`: an engineering estimate, not a
  certification.

Validation (OpenFOAM v2406, default `medium` mesh): Hagen–Poiseuille pipe
D 10 mm, L 200 mm, Re 20: 0.1327 Pa vs 0.1273 Pa (+4.2% including inlet
development), centreline 1.99 × mean. Sphere at Re 50: Cd 1.594 vs
Schiller–Naumann 1.542 (+3.4%).

## Toolchain

OpenFOAM is not bundled (GPL). Discovery: `KERNELCAD_OPENFOAM` (a wrapper
like `/usr/bin/openfoam2406`, `native` or `docker`) → `simpleFoam` on PATH →
an `openfoamNNNN` wrapper → a LOCAL Docker image (`KERNELCAD_OPENFOAM_IMAGE`,
default `opencfd/openfoam-run:2406`, about 250 MB download / 1 GB on disk; never
pulled implicitly). Containers run with `--network none`. Missing →
`cfd.solver.unavailable` with the install command.

Solver processes: `cores` (default 1, capped by `KERNELCAD_CFD_MAX_CORES`,
default 2). Each run is keyed by a hash of the generated case: calling
`run_cfd` again with the same inputs returns the finished result
(`reused: 'finished'`) or waits on the live run (`reused: 'joined'`), so a
client that timed out can simply call again. `cfd_summary({ output_dir })`
reads a stored summary, or the progress stage of a run still going.

`output_dir` keeps the case (`case/system`, `case/constant/triSurface/geometry.stl`,
logs), `cfd-summary.json`, `cfd-result.json` and the PNG; `export_vtk: true`
adds `case/VTK` (foamToVTK) for ParaView.

skills.desc: Export 2D engineering-drawing sheets (SVG, or a printable PDF on a standard sheet) from any model or assembly — third-angle front/top/left + isometric views with hidden-line removal, overall dimensions, and a title block. Use when the deliverable is a human-readable fabrication or review drawing.
skills.body:
---
name: kernelcad-drawings
description: Export 2D engineering-drawing sheets (SVG, or a printable PDF on a standard sheet) from any model or assembly — third-angle front/top/left + isometric views with hidden-line removal, overall dimensions, and a title block. Use when the deliverable is a human-readable fabrication or review drawing.
---

# kernelCAD — engineering drawings

`export({ target: 'model', format: 'svg-drawing' })` renders a `.kcad.ts` model as a standard third-angle engineering-drawing sheet in SVG. It works on single bodies and on assemblies (`assembly.model()` / `solvedModel(...)`) — assembly parts are projected together in world frame, so one part occluding another renders correctly as hidden lines.

## What the sheet contains

- **Views**: front, top (above front), left (left of front) — third-angle arrangement with shared-axis alignment — plus an isometric pictorial in the upper-right cell. One drawing scale for all views, snapped to the standard series (…, 2:1, 1:1, 1:2, 1:5, …) and stamped in the title block.
- **Line styling** per drafting convention: visible edges solid full-weight; hidden edges dashed half-weight; tangent edges (fillet boundaries, smooth face transitions) thin solid. The isometric view omits hidden lines.
- **Dimensions**: by default the overall bounding box — width (under the front view), height (right of the front view), depth (left of the top view), with extension lines and arrowheads. Values are model millimetres. Author your own with `annotations` (below) to dimension actual features instead.
- **Title block**: model name, scale, units (mm), date, and the third-angle projection symbol.
- Coincident projected segments (e.g. a bore's front and back rim landing on the same arc) are deduplicated visible-first — nothing renders twice or dashed underneath a solid line.

## PDF sheet for the shop

`format: 'pdf-drawing'` writes the same sheet as a vector PDF ready to print or send: the views, hidden lines, dimensions, hole callouts and GD&T are the SVG sheet's, transcribed page for page. It adds a standard sheet and a full title block:

- **Sheet**: `sheet` is `'a4'` `'a3'` (default) `'a2'` `'a1'` `'a0'` or `'ansi-a'` … `'ansi-e'`, always landscape; `'auto'` / `'auto-ansi'` pick the smallest sheet that holds the views at 1:1, else the largest one with a reduced scale. The scale is snapped to the standard series and printed in the title block. Section views take room inside the sheet instead of growing the page.
- **Projection**: `projection: 'third'` (default) or `'first'`. First angle puts the top view below the front view, the left view right of it, the isometric lower-left, and draws the first-angle symbol; automatic dimensions move to each view's free side.
- **Title block**: TITLE (`title`, default the model name), PART NAME (`partName`), MATERIAL (`material`, default the shared material of the assembly parts), REV (`revision`), SCALE, UNITS, SHEET size, DATE (`date`, default today). { "tool": "export", "input": { "target": "model", "file": "bracket.kcad.ts", "format": "pdf-drawing", "output_path": "out/bracket.pdf",

The generic `export` tool supports optional `visualQa` on both `svg-drawing`
and `pdf-drawing`. It inspects the **serialized** sheet, not only the CAD
model. For PDFs it also reads back page size, vector content and the text layer.
The default export path remains unchanged unless `visualQa` is supplied.

```json
{ "tool": "export", "input": { "target": "model", "file": "bracket.kcad.ts", "format": "pdf-drawing",
  "output_path": "out/bracket-reviewed.pdf",
  "options": { "format": "pdf-drawing", "sheet": "a4", "visualQa": { "autoRepair": true, "maxAttempts": 3 } } } }
```

Read `drawingReport.visualQa` from the export result. The report includes
`status` (`verified`, `needs-review`, or `incomplete`), issue codes and
sheet locations, the list of rejected/accepted attempts, and a separate PDF
readback report. A `verified` result requires a **complete declared critical-dimension review**
and passing layout checks. Without a declared critical-dimension contract, the
result remains `incomplete` even if every layout check passes. An unresolved
critical dimension or drawing decision results in `needs-review`. None of these
statuses certifies physical fit, tolerances, or manufacturing-standard compliance.

The repair loop first moves annotations already reported as crowded using the
existing offset option, then tries progressively larger ISO/ANSI sheet sizes.
It accepts only measurable reductions in layout issues and stops after at most
three retries. It never changes source 3D geometry, dimension values, or
unresolved engineering decisions. A missing critical dimension remains a
blocking finding even after a successful layout repair. Review any remaining
issues before releasing a drawing externally.

```json

```


Pass via `options` (MCP) — all optional:

`{ format: 'svg-drawing', options: { format: 'svg-drawing', sheet: 'a3' } }`.
Omitting `options.format` fails with `export.options-format-mismatch`.
Inspect the exported artifact rather than assuming an unknown option was
honoured. In particular, confirm the actual view count for a front-view-only
request; the default sheet contains four views.

- `sheet`: `'a4'` (default, 297×210 landscape), `'a3'` (420×297), or any `pdf-drawing` size (`'a2'` … `'ansi-e'`, `'auto'`).
- `views: ['front']`: a single centred front elevation with width/height dimensions. Omit `views` for the default four-view sheet. Author front-view annotations explicitly for feature dimensions. A front-only drawing rejects annotations assigned to absent views and isometric-only balloons or exploded overlays.
- `projection`: `'third'` (default) or `'first'` — see "PDF sheet for the shop".
- `titleBlock`: `{ title?, partName?, material?, revision? }` — switches to the full title block the PDF sheet uses.
- `zoneGrid`: `boolean` (default `false`) — when `true`, adds an ISO 5457 zone reference border frame with vertical letters (`A..D`), horizontal numbers (`1..N`), and a margin sheet-size stamp. Works on both `svg-drawing` and `pdf-drawing`.
- `modelName`: title-block name; defaults to the script's file name.
- `date`: title-block date string; defaults to a placeholder so output stays byte-deterministic (stamp an ISO date when the drawing is released).
- `annotations`: authored dimensions and notes — see below.
- `sections`: cutting-plane section views — see "Section views" below.
- `exploded`: `{ factor, mode }` — explode the isometric cell (`mode` is `mate-axis` or `radial`). Ortho views stay assembled.
- `balloons`: item balloons on the isometric cell; numbers match BOM item numbers from `inspect({ of: 'bom' })`.
- `partsList`: parts-list table (item, name, qty, material) above the title block, from the same BOM rows.

```json

```

## Declared functional review

Declare `.dimension({ id: 'width', kind: 'linear', from: [0,0,0], to: [80,0,0] })`
and `.drawingReview({ id: 'mount', requirements: [{ id: 'width', featureId: 'plate interface',
annotationId: 'authored:width', expectedKind: 'linear', role: 'critical', reason: 'Mating width' }], decisions: [] })`
on the source shape. Plans follow that shape into downstream exports and add no geometry.
`featureId` describes engineering intent; it is not a topology reference.

Mechanical SVG/PDF options support `reviewPlans` (additional plans, merged with source plans),
`decisionResolutions` and `requireCompleteReview`. A plan needs nonempty `id`, both arrays,
and at least one requirement or decision. Unknown fields and duplicate IDs reject.
Each requirement targets an exact authored ID and measurable kind: `linear`, `diameter`,
`radius` or `angular`. Notes, datum symbols and automatic rows cannot satisfy it.

`drawing_report.review` / runtime `drawingReport.review` contains `status`, `requirements`,
`decisions`, `criticalCount`, `coveredCriticalCount`, `decisionCount` and `unresolvedDecisionCount`.
Requirements include plan/requirement IDs, feature, reason, annotation ID, expected kind, role
and `missing`, `ambiguous`, `kind-mismatch`, `hidden`, `crowded`, `label-overridden` or `covered`
status. Failed reference requirements are advisories. Failed critical requirements and every
unresolved decision block `complete`; no plan means `not-declared`.

Decisions declare `{ id, kind: 'datum'|'fit'|'tolerance'|'dimension'|'other', featureId, prompt,
resolution?: { note, provenance } }`. To override a source decision resolution, use
`decisionResolutions: { [drawingDecisionKey(planId, decisionId)]: { note, provenance } }`;
the key is `encodeURIComponent(planId) + ':' + encodeURIComponent(decisionId)`.
Both resolution strings must be nonempty; unknown keys and malformed overrides reject.
A resolution records intent/provenance only; it does not create geometry or GD&T.

Review evaluates final rendered rows after suppression and layout. A manual critical text
replacement blocks coverage; restore the computed label or revise the source declaration.
`requireCompleteReview: true` refuses incomplete and undeclared exports. Ordinary exports
remain available with truthful incomplete reports/warnings. Printable SVG (`pdfSheet: true`)
and PDF use the same review report. Architectural style rejects supplied review contracts.
Declared geometric callout coverage does not certify physical fit, tolerances or manufacture.

## Annotations — dimensioning what you actually care about

Without `autoAnnotate`, the default dimensions state the overall bounding box. `autoAnnotate: true` derives feature callouts and positions from the B-rep. `annotations` lets you select exact features and declare the dimensions you need. Supplying authored annotations replaces the default bounding-box dimensions; automatic annotations can be requested separately.

Every entry shares four optional fields: `view` (`front` default, or `top` / `left` / `iso`), `text` (override the computed label), and `offset` (extra sheet-millimetres pushing the annotation further from the geometry). The rest is per `kind`:

| `kind` | geometry | label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `linear` | `from`, `to` anchors, optional `tol` | distance along the dominant view axis, optionally `± 0.1` / `+0.2/−0.05` / `H7` |
| `radius` | `edge` (an EdgeQuery selecting a circular edge) | `R<r>` |
| `diameter` | `edge` (ditto) | `⌀<d>` |
| `angular` | `from`, `to` EdgeQueries — the apex is where the two edges cross in that view | `<deg>°` |
| `note` | `at` anchor + required `text` | your text, on a leader |
| `hole` | `edge` (rim), one of `through: true` / `depth`, optional `counterbore`/`countersink`/`count` | `⌀6.5 THRU`, blind `⌀6.5 ▾ 10`, `⌴⌀12 ▾ 4` / `⌵⌀12 × 90°` suffixes, `4× ` pattern prefix |
| `fillet` | `edge` (a circular fillet boundary arc) | `R<r>` |
| `chamfer` | `edge` (anchor) + required `size`, optional `angleDeg` (default 45) | `<size> × <angle>°` |
| `datum` | `face` (a FaceQuery) + required `label` | ASME square datum-feature symbol with the letter |
| `fcf` | one of `edge`/`face` + `type` (`position`\|`flatness`\|`perpendicularity`\|`parallelism`\|`concentricity`\|`cylindricity`) + `value`, optional `datums`/`modifier` | feature control frame: type symbol · value(±modifier) · datum letters |
| `baseline` | `origin` anchor, non-empty `targets` anchors, `axis` (`'x'`\|`'y'`), optional `side` (`'positive'`\|`'negative'`), `tol`, `prefix` | stacked dimension lines from one shared datum extension line along the view axis (ISO 129-1 / ASME Y14.5) |
| `ordinate` | `origin` anchor, non-empty `targets` anchors, `axis` (`'x'`\|`'y'`), optional `side`, `originLabel` (default `'0'`), `prefix` | running perpendicular witness lines (no arrowheads, automatic jogs when adjacent labels would collide) labeled with distances from origin |

`baseline` and `ordinate` reject empty `targets`, invalid `axis`/`side`, or unresolvable anchors with an error rather than dropping dimensions. Both render identically in `svg-drawing` and `pdf-drawing`.

```json
{ "kind": "baseline", "view": "front", "axis": "x", "origin": [0, 0, 0], "targets": [[20, 0, 0], [50, 0, 0], [80, 0, 0]], "tol": 0.1 }
{ "kind": "ordinate", "view": "top", "axis": "x", "origin": [0, 0, 0], "targets": [[10, 10, 0], [12, 10, 0], [60, 10, 0]], "originLabel": "0" }
```

`chamfer`'s `size` is author-supplied rather than measured — a bare edge query carries no feature history, so the chamfer leg length isn't recoverable from geometry alone at export time. `hole` requires exactly one of `through`/`depth` — the export fails loudly (naming the annotation) if both or neither are set, same honesty contract as every other annotation kind.

```json
{ "kind": "hole", "view": "top", "edge": { "ofCurveType": "CIRCLE", "near": [10, 10, 0] }, "through": true, "counterbore": { "diameter": 12, "depth": 4 } }
{ "kind": "fcf", "view": "top", "edge": { "ofCurveType": "CIRCLE", "near": [70, 40, 0] }, "type": "position", "value": 0.1, "datums": ["A"], "modifier": "⌀" }
```

An **anchor** is an explicit model point `[x, y, z]`, `{ edge: EdgeQuery }` (resolves to the edge's curve midpoint), or `{ face: FaceQuery }` (resolves to the face centre) — the same selector vocabulary `fillet` / `chamfer` / `selectEdge` use.

```json
{
  "options": {
    "format": "svg-drawing",
    "annotations": [
      { "kind": "linear", "from": [0, 0, 0], "to": [60, 0, 0] },
      { "kind": "linear", "from": { "face": { "atZ": 0 } }, "to": { "face": { "atZ": 10 } } },
      { "kind": "diameter", "view": "top", "edge": { "ofCurveType": "CIRCLE", "atZ": 10 } },
      { "kind": "angular",
        "from": { "ofCurveType": "LINE", "near": [20, 0, 0], "within": { "zMin": -0.5, "zMax": 0.5 } },
        "to":   { "ofCurveType": "LINE", "near": [0, 0, 15], "within": { "xMin": -0.5, "xMax": 0.5 } } },
      { "kind": "note", "at": { "face": { "atZ": 10 } }, "text": "BREAK ALL EDGES 0.5" }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Placement rules

- **Anchoring is in model space.** Anchors resolve to 3D model points and are pushed through the same projection + sheet transform as the geometry, so a dimension stays welded to its feature when the drawing scale changes.
- **Text and leaders are sheet-constant.** Label height, arrowheads, leader stems and dimension-line spacing are fixed sheet millimetres at every scale — only positions scale.
- **Stacking is deterministic and author-ordered.** Annotations bucket by (view, side): a `linear` whose projected span is wider than tall goes *below* its view, otherwise *right* of it. Within a bucket the first sits 8 mm out and each further one steps 8 mm further; angular arcs grow by 8 mm; leaders rotate 30° per leader. Reordering the model cannot reshuffle the sheet — only reordering the array can. View captions move down automatically to clear whatever stacks beneath them.

### Failure behaviour

An annotation whose query matches **zero** edges/faces, matches **more than one** without a `near` disambiguator, asks for a radius on a non-circular edge, or measures an angle between edges that are parallel in that view, **fails the export** with a `feature.selection.no-match` diagnostic naming `annotations[i]` and the reason. All failures are reported at once. Nothing is silently dropped: a drawing that quietly omits a dimension you asked for is worse than one that errors.

## Conventions and behaviour

- Model space is mm, z-up; the front view looks along +y (model front faces −y), matching the canonical render pose.
- The SVG is structured for downstream tooling: `<g id="view-front|top|left|iso">` per view with `class="visible|hidden|tangent"` subgroups, `data-kc-scale` / `data-kc-units` on the root element.
- Curved edges are sampled to polylines at 0.02 mm chord tolerance — invisible at print scale.
- A drawing is a derived artifact, not source-of-truth: change the `.kcad.ts`, re-export.

## Section views

`options.sections: [{ plane, label }]` cuts the assembled body with a real half-space boolean (not a render-time visual clip) and adds a section-view cell below the standard 4-view grid — the sheet grows taller to make room; the standard views are pixel-for-pixel unaffected.

```json
{
  "options": {
    "format": "svg-drawing",
    "sections": [{ "plane": "xy", "label": "A" }]
  }
}
```

- `plane`: `'xy'` (cuts along Z), `'xz'` (cuts along Y), `'yz'` (cuts along X) — position defaults to the bounding-box midpoint on that axis — or `{ origin: [x,y,z], normal: [nx,ny,nz] }` for an explicit position. Any non-zero normal is supported; oblique cuts get an auxiliary view looking straight at the cut.
- The kept half is the far-from-viewer side (the ASME convention — remove the near material, look straight at the cut). The section view reuses the standard camera for that axis (`'top'` for an `'xy'` cut, `'front'` for `'xz'`, `'left'` for `'yz'`), so it renders through the same HLR pipeline (visible/hidden/tangent styling) as every other view.
- The true cut cross-section — the face(s) that land exactly on the cutting plane — is filled with a 45° hatch pattern (`fill="url(#kc-section-hatch)"`). A hole the plane slices through renders correctly as a hole in the hatch (outer + inner wire, `fill-rule="evenodd"`), not a solid disk.
- A cutting-plane indicator (dashed line, arrows, the section letter at both ends) is drawn on the "parent" view where the plane appears edge-on (`'front'` for an `'xy'`/`'yz'` cut, `'top'` for an `'xz'` cut).
- A plane that doesn't pass through the body's bounding box fails with `drawing.section.plane-misses-body`.
- The section cell is captioned `SECTION A-A` (from `label`).

## Architectural floor plans

A building or room model drawn with the default (mechanical) style gets part
annotations — datums, flatness, ISO 2768 — that mean nothing on a floor plan,
and the export warns `drawing.style.architectural-suggested`. Pass
`style: 'architectural'` (svg-drawing or pdf-drawing) for a plan instead:

```json
{ "options": { "format": "pdf-drawing", "style": "architectural", "title": "Cabin",
  "plan": { "rooms": [{ "name": "Living", "at": [1000, 1000] }], "northDeg": 30 } } }
```

- The whole model is fused and cut 1 m (3'-6" imperial) above the finished floor — the top of the largest upward face in the bottom quarter of the model, else its lowest point. `plan.cutHeight` (mm above the floor) moves the cut.
- Cut walls are filled; everything below the cut (sills, floor edges) is drawn thin from above. Openings at the cut height (doors, windows with a sill below the cut) are gaps.
- Dimensions: a chain of wall and opening widths along each exterior side (read just inside the outermost wall face), plus the overall length and width.
- Rooms are the enclosed floor regions of a section. Door openings join rooms at the cut height, so rooms are read from whichever section (the cut, or 2.0–2.5 m above the floor, above the door heads) encloses the most. Each gets its name (the room containing `plan.rooms[i].at`, else `ROOM n`) and net area (m², or ft²).
- Units: millimetres, or feet-inches (to 1/4") when the model's overall size and wall height are whole feet / inches. Force with `plan.units: 'metric' | 'imperial'`. The scale is the largest architectural scale that fits (1:20 … 1:2000, or 1/2" … 1/32" = 1'-0"); `sheet: 'auto'` picks the smallest sheet that holds 1:100 (1/8" = 1'-0").
- A scale bar, a north arrow (`plan.northDeg`, clockwise from sheet up) and a title block (title, scale, units, sheet, date, revision) complete the sheet. The mechanical-only keys (`annotations`, `sections`, `autoAnnotate`, `exploded`, `balloons`, `partsList`) do not apply.

## Drafting profiles and annotation review

Both drawing formats accept `draftingProfile: 'general' | 'machining' | 'sheet-metal'`, or a JSON profile with `id`, `name`, and optional `sheet`, `projection`, `dimensioningStyle`, `tolerance`, and `notes`. Omitted custom settings default to A4, third angle, and baseline. Explicit export settings take precedence. Named presets supply drafting preferences, not a certified process or approved engineering tolerance; the existing automatic tolerance defaults still apply unless you set them.

Baseline locations share a datum origin; chain locations measure consecutive positions; symmetry dimensions verified mirrored positions from a center cue and falls back to baseline for asymmetric layouts; ordinate emits running perpendicular coordinate witness lines from the part datum edge (`0` plus each coordinate, with automatic collision jogs). Explicit `autoAnnotate.datums: [{ label, face }]` overrides heuristic automatic datum selection.
