| `kinematic.checkStaticHold(arm, opts)` | Can the declared actuator hold this joint against gravity? | `assembly.joint.static-hold.exceeded`, `assembly.joint.static-hold.margin-low`, `assembly.joint.static-hold.no-actuator`, `assembly.joint.static-hold.mass-unavailable`, `kinematic.static-hold.no-actuator-declared` |
| `kinematic.motionLoad(arm, opts)` | What wrench does each driven joint carry along the animation / joint range / named poses? | `mechanism.load.torque-exceeded`, `mechanism.load.torque-margin-low`, `mechanism.load.side-load-exceeded`, `mechanism.load.not-resolved` |
| `kinematic.sweepTolerance({ code\|file, params, gates, boundaryTolerance?, boundaryBudget? })` | Where does the design fail across a parameter range, and which ledger requirement is binding there? | `kinematic.sweep-tolerance.combo-cap-exceeded`, `kinematic.sweep-tolerance.boundary-budget-exhausted` (plus whatever the swept gates/requirements emit per combo) |

`checkLoadCapacity` defaults to the closed-form beam check. Its deprecated
`mode: 'stub'` compatibility path compares manually supplied per-part loads
against a mate's deprecated `maxLoad`; for a mated assembly, connector and
part-frame origins use the solved mate placements. This is a lever-arm sanity
check, not reaction propagation, FEA, or hardware acceptance. A warning with
`assembly.joint.load-unverified` means a connector origin could not be resolved
by this synchronous path, or a declared load rating is unsupported (the legacy
checker does not compare torque ratings on ball mates), so that capacity
comparison did not run. See the [Gate 3 solved-frame replay bundle](../../../../docs/demos/issue-917-gate3-solved-frame/README.md),
the [topology-origin unverified replay bundle](../../../../docs/demos/joint-load-unverified-topology-1272/README.md),
and the [ball-joint torque replay bundle](../../../../docs/demos/joint-load-ball-torque-1272/README.md).

### `checkStaticHold` — gravitational holding torque vs actuator capacity

Per actuated joint (revolute/prismatic with a declared `actuator: { torqueNm
| forceN }` on `arm.revolute(...)`/`arm.prismatic(...)`), samples a pose grid
(or an explicit `opts.pose`) and computes the gravitational torque/force the
actuator must supply to hold the downstream mass still, using real mass
properties (volume and center of mass from the part's declared `density`/`material`,
same substrate as `inspect({ of: 'mass' })`). Reports the worst pose,
required torque/force, declared capacity, and margin percent.
Coverage is limited to actuated `arm.revolute(...)` and `arm.prismatic(...)`
joints. Mate-only `mechanicalJoint` chains are not evaluated. When no
actuated body-tree joint is selected, the result is `ok: false` with an
`assembly.joint.static-hold.no-actuator` warning, naming moving mates when
available; this result has no holding-capacity coverage. If the assembly
cannot be lowered to measure part mass, the result is `ok: false` with
`assembly.joint.static-hold.mass-unavailable`; an unavailable load measurement
cannot pass. Demo and replay bundle: [Issue #1270 static-hold coverage](../../../../docs/demos/issue-1270-static-hold/README.md) · [mass-unavailable regression](../../../../docs/demos/static-hold-mass-unavailable/README.md).
`opts.minTorqueMarginPct` (default 20) is a floor, not a hard pass/fail — a
joint that clears capacity but misses the margin still returns `ok: true`
with a `margin-low` warn diagnostic; an exceeded capacity or missing actuator
coverage returns `ok: false`. v1 assumes rigid links and a single uniform
gravity vector; pair with `checkLoadCapacity` for applied external loads.

### `sweepTolerance` — range proofs over the requirements ledger

Declares one or more `param()` names as `{ values: [...] }` or `{ min, max,
steps }`, expands the cartesian product (capped at 64 combos —
`kinematic.sweep-tolerance.combo-cap-exceeded` fires and truncates past the
cap), and re-evaluates the script per combo via the same `set_param` +
`evaluate_script` path an agent would use manually. Per combo it measures
**every requirement in the S2 ledger** — script `require()` declarations,
`dfmSpec` gates, gated `feaStudy.minSafetyFactor` and mechanical intent —
plus `interference` + `mountingHoles` + `jointAxis` (all default on, fold out
of one `validateAssemblyWithMates` call) and `reachable` when
`gates.reachable: { tipLink, targetPosition, targetOrientation? }` is
declared. A `not-evaluated` ledger entry never counts as green.

After the coarse grid, each numeric pass/fail transition is bisected down to
`boundaryTolerance` (default 0.001, absolute parameter units) and reported in
`boundaries[]`: the parameter, direction, pass/fail values, the failing side,
and `bindingRequirements` / `bindingGates` naming what actually flips. The
message reads like "`wall` fails below 1.840 Wall; binding: `wall`". Each
boundary consumes `boundaryBudget` evaluations (default 64; 0 disables
bisection); an exhausted budget emits
`kinematic.sweep-tolerance.boundary-budget-exhausted` and reports the final
bracket as an interval, never a proven edge. Choice/string params are swept as
discrete points and are not bisected.

Returns `results[]` (one row per combo: `{ combo, gates, requirements,
verdict, diagnostics }`), `firstFailure[gateName]`,
`firstRequirementFailure[requirementName]`, `boundaries[]`, and a
`coverage` block whose statement is "checked at N points plus boundaries;
sampled, not a proof". Hole diameters bound through a ParamRef
(`.hole({ diameter: someParam })`) resolve to the combo's evaluated value, so
sweeping that diameter produces a real pass/fail envelope.

## MCP tools (one per facade entry)

Every facade entry has a paired MCP tool that accepts the same shape from an
agent context. The tools load the `.kcad.ts` source, run it, capture the
named assembly off the script's session, and dispatch to the facade.

- `verify({ check: 'mounting-holes' })` — wraps the facade; accepts `file` or `code`
- `verify({ check: 'assembly-path', file|code, assembly?, directions?, disassemblyOrder?, sequence?, threadedFasteners?, stability?, gravity?, fixtures?, contactToleranceMm? })` — continuous mesh straight-removal check along six world axes plus explicit vectors; per-part valid directions/blockers and three-way states (removable / blocked / unknown), optional greedy order/stuck set, and a `sequence: true` build plan with a model stamp. Fastened/fixed clusters become subassemblies planned recursively inside and installed as one unit; deterministic heuristics order valid steps; stuck sets use a budgeted partition and a sampling fallback labelled found-by-search, never proven. Threaded fasteners are `unknown: non-straight-path` until P2. `stability: true` adds the approximate P3 centre-of-mass/support-polygon check (`needsHold`, `Step.heldBy`, `model.stability`) under a declared `gravity`/`fixtures`; it is not a physics simulation. Contact is conservative; no rotation, inferred axes or hardware certification.
- `verify({ check: 'swept-collision' })` — wraps the facade; accepts `file|code`, `joint`, `range`, `collision_tolerance_mm3`
- `verify({ check: 'joint-range' })` — wraps `suggestJointRanges`; accepts `file|code`, `assembly`, `joint`, `search`, `clearance_mm` (default 0.3), `step`, `resolution`. Passing `{ sweep_budget }` sets the face-weighted exact BREP distance budget. Each revolute or prismatic joint is walked alone from its authored pose while other mates stay at their authored poses. Exact BREP distance brackets the first non-exempt pair inside the clearance, and the reported stop is the clear side of that bracket so the suggested limit keeps the requested clearance. Returns the stop, the limiting part pair, the resolution, and `stop` | `no-stop` | `unknown`. `no-stop` means no crossing was found at the sampled poses, not continuous proof that the interval is clear. A missing finite bound, the sweep budget, or a failed measurement is `unknown`, never a clear side. The `limitsSnippet` is for the caller to apply; the script is not rewritten. Mate neighbours, declared contact pairs, and `disableCollision` pairs are not stops. A contact thinner than the coarse step can be missed. Demo: `docs/demos/joint-range-suggestion/README.md`.
- `verify({ check: 'reachable' })` — wraps the facade; accepts `file|code`, `tip_link`, `target_position`, `target_orientation`, `prefer_solver`, `max_iterations`, `seed`
- `verify({ check: 'load-capacity' })` — wraps the facade; accepts `file|code`, `loads`, `materials`, `mode`, `safety_factor_threshold`
- `verify({ check: 'static-hold' })` — wraps the facade; accepts `file|code`, `joint`, `pose`, `gravity`, `min_torque_margin_pct`, `range_samples`
- `verify({ check: 'physics' })` — full mechanism truth with physics engine: kinematic disconnect / interference / DOF checks plus static equilibrium and drop-on-release under gravity. Scalar `coupleMates` outputs are derived from sampled source mates, represented by native joint equality constraints, and checked at every release integration observation (`mechanism.coupling-residual` if the relation exceeds tolerance). Accepts `file|code`, `assembly`, `physics: false` to skip physics engine. Returns `{ ok, mechanism, failures, coverage }`. A closed-loop mate graph or unmappable coupling returns `mechanism: 'unverified'` with warning `mechanism.physics-unsupported` (coverage.physics false). This is unsupported physics mapping, not a dynamics failure, and it is not a verified build. A ratio check does not simulate involute tooth contact or certify a gear mesh.
- `verify({ check: 'motion-load' })` — mate assemblies: loads on every `mechanicalJoint` along the animationView tracks (gravity + inertia + external forces passed as motion_loads), or quasi-static over the joint limits (motion_mode: 'range'). Reports peak torque vs `torqueNm` (margin < 1x error, < 2x warning), actuator-shaft axial / radial / bending loads (checked only against `radialLimitN` / `axialLimitN`), the radial load per support (up to two coaxial supports, each at the station where it bears on the shaft: its connector on the joint axis, else the middle of its material nearest the shaft; an ambiguous station is a warning, not a number), the worst pose, a torque-vs-time series, and `partLoads` (the worst wrench per part and side in that part's frame). The script-level `kinematic.motionLoad` returns the same envelope; feed `partLoads` to `feaStudy({ loadsFrom: { motion, part } })` to solve a structural safety factor at that pose with no hand-typed load. Use `supports: { '<joint>': ['servo'] }` to see the shaft side load without a bushing. Declare a purchased part's mass with `arm.part(name, shape, { massKg })`.
- `sweep_tolerance` — standalone tool (not a `verify` check — it surveys an envelope rather than gating one state); accepts `file|code`, `params`, `gates`, `boundaryTolerance`, `boundaryBudget`
- `verify({ check: 'assembly' })` (extended) — composes the four `verify`-routed checks when called with `gates: ['kinematic']`

## Recovery loop — code → nextAction → repair

Every emitted diagnostic carries a structured `nextAction` field describing
the smallest repair likely to clear the gate. Use the table below to pick a
repair, edit the `.kcad.ts` source, then re-run the same `kinematic.check*`
call to confirm.

| Code | `nextAction.kind` | Typical recovery |
|------|------|----|
| K1 `kinematic.collision.swept` | `rewrite-feature` | Inspect `result.collidingPoses[]`; narrow joint limits OR reshape the colliding part OR insert clearance |
| K2 `kinematic.collision.swept.sample-density-warning` | `fix-arg` (`opts.range`) | Halve the step size OR widen the range |
| `kinematic.collision.swept.unmeasured` | `rewrite-feature` | A sampled pose was not lowered or its exact boolean failed; see `result.walks[].unknown`, simplify the named parts or change the step, and re-run |
| K3 `kinematic.unreachable` | conditional by `axis` | `axis: 'position' \| 'both'` → restructure (lengthen link, add DOF, move target). `axis: 'orientation'` → relax orientation tolerance or drop the orientation constraint |
| K4 `kinematic.reachability.iteration-cap-hit` | `fix-arg` (`opts.maxIterations`) | Bump iterations OR relax tolerances; inspect `closestApproach` to choose |
| K5 `kinematic.solver.unsupported-config` | `rewrite-feature` | Switch `preferSolver: 'numeric'`: the closed-form solver takes serial spherical-wrist chains only (closed loops go through the numeric path) |
| `kinematic.loop.lockup` | `rewrite-feature` | The loop cannot close past the named pose (dead point / range limit). Limit the driven range to the last closed pose, or change link lengths |
| `kinematic.loop.branch-flip` | `rewrite-feature` | The loop went over center (or a `loopMode` pin could not hold). If intended, that pose IS the over-center point; else narrow the range or pin the branch |
| `kinematic.loop.mobility-mismatch` | `fix-arg` (`poses`) | Drive exactly as many loop joints as `mobility` reports (`solve_mates` → `loop.mobility[].independent` lists a valid set) |
| `kinematic.loop.branch-ambiguous` | `rewrite-feature` | The loop is modeled flat/straight; add `arm.loopMode(loop, { joint, sign })` or model it away from the singular pose |
| K6 `kinematic.load-exceeds-yield` | `rewrite-feature` | Thicken the cross-section, change material, shorten the moment arm |
| K7 `kinematic.load.beam-not-applicable` | `fix-arg` (`crossSection`) | Add the part's `crossSection` declaration; only beam-shaped parts qualify for the closed-form path |
| K8 `kinematic.no-material-declared` | `fix-arg` (`opts.materials`) | Add `materials: { partName: { material: 'steel' \| 'aluminum' \| 'pla' \| 'abs' \| 'pet' } }` for every loaded part |
| K9 `kinematic.mounting-hole.diameter-mismatch` | `fix-arg` | Set both connectors' hole diameter to the same value |
| `assembly.joint.static-hold.exceeded` | `rewrite-feature` | Increase the actuator torque/force to the value named in the message, or shorten/lighten the downstream link |
| `assembly.joint.static-hold.margin-low` | `rewrite-feature` | Increase the actuator torque/force for the requested margin, or shorten/lighten the downstream link |
| `assembly.joint.static-hold.no-actuator` | `rewrite-feature` | Declare `actuator: { torqueNm }` on `arm.revolute(...)` or `actuator: { forceN }` on `arm.prismatic(...)`; mate-only `mechanicalJoint` chains are not covered; check their `torqueNm` ratings with `verify({ check: 'motion-load', quasi_static: true })` |
| `assembly.joint.static-hold.mass-unavailable` | `rewrite-feature` | Repair the assembly geometry or lowering failure so static-hold can measure part mass properties |
| `kinematic.static-hold.no-actuator-declared` | `fix-arg` (`actuator`) | Add `actuator: { torqueNm }` (revolute) / `{ forceN }` (prismatic) to the joint declaration |
| `mechanism.load.torque-exceeded` / `mechanism.load.torque-margin-low` | `rewrite-feature` | Stronger actuator, lighter/shorter links, or slower motion (aim for 2x) |
| `mechanism.load.side-load-exceeded` | `rewrite-feature` | Add a coaxial bushing/bearing and list it in the mechanicalJoint `supports` |
| `mechanism.load.not-resolved` | `fix-arg` (`supports`) | At most two coaxial supports at different heights; no closed loop through the joint; a support that touches the shaft at two stations or not at all: name the part that bears (the bushing), or add a connector on the joint axis where it bears |
| `kinematic.sweep-tolerance.combo-cap-exceeded` | `fix-arg` (`params`) | Narrow the swept ranges/values, or split the sweep into multiple calls |

## Trade-off note on K2 sparse-sampling

K2 is a signal, not a hard cap. The sweep still ran end-to-end; the warning is
that the (range, step) you supplied falls below the safe floor (36 samples for
revolute, 25 for prismatic) and the sweep may have stepped over a narrow
collision window. Agents can ignore K2 for fast-prototyping iteration; for a
production design review, never ignore K2 — re-run with a tighter step.

## Boundary

This skill is feasibility-checking. CAD authoring stays on
`kernelcad-authoring`. Visualization stays on the renderer. To *fix* a flagged
mechanism, return to `kernelcad-authoring` to edit the `.kcad.ts` source, then
re-run the relevant `kinematic.check*` to confirm.

## Range-based vs timeline-based motion verification

Two interference checks cover motion, answering different questions — pick by
what you are validating:

- **Range-based swept collision (this skill)** —
  `kinematic.checkSweptCollision(arm, opts)` / the `verify({ check: 'swept-collision' })` MCP
  tool sweep ONE joint across its full `range` at a sample density and ask "is
  any pose in this joint's whole envelope a collision?" Use it as a feasibility
  gate while designing the mechanism — it does not care about timing, easing,
  or how multiple joints move together.

- **Timeline-based animation verification (`kernelcad-authoring`)** —
  `kernelcad animate` / the `capture_animation` MCP tool verify the specific
  multi-track poses an `animationView({...})` timeline actually visits
  (keyframe times + segment midpoints, eases and dwells included), then capture
  the MP4/frames. Use it to confirm a particular authored MOTION (several joints
  moving on a shared timeline) stays clear and to produce the motion artifact.

Both reuse the mechanism-validity interference rule (overlap > 0.01 mm³ and thicker than 0.01 mm; thinner is face contact) and honor
declared `solvedModel({ ignore })` pairs, so a pose clean under one is judged by
the same rule under the other. Range-based proves the joint's envelope is safe;
timeline-based proves the choreographed cycle is safe and renders it.

## Non-robotics mechanism coverage

These four calls work on any moving assembly, not just robot arms:

- **Linkages** — 4-bar, slider-crank, scissor jacks, toggle clamps: author
  the real closed loop with mates and drive only the input joint (see
  "Closed loops" below; `09-four-bar-loop-swept`)
- **Latches** — over-center, pawl-ratchet (`checkSweptCollision` over the
  latch handle reports the over-center point; `checkReachable` for the
  locking-pin engagement target — `06-over-center-latch-reachable`)
- **Hinges** — laptop clamshell, butterfly knife (`checkSweptCollision` over
  the hinge angle)
- **Gear trains and escapements** — tooth clearance, pawl engagement
  (`checkSweptCollision` over the driven-wheel rotation; `checkLoadCapacity`
  for the spring torque)
- **Scissor jacks** — the true closed loop (two crossed links, two sliders)
  swept over the lift angle (`04-scissor-jack-swept`); do not invent
  `joint.scissorLift`

## Closed loops

Closed mate loops are solved, not refused. The solver builds a spanning tree
from the grounded (first) part; every mate the tree leaves out closes one
loop, and **the loop is named after that mate**. Closure of the cut mate is a
residual (revolute: pivots meet and axes align; prismatic: no rotation, no
off-axis offset; ball: pivots meet; fastened: all six), solved by damped least
squares.

- **Drive only the input.** Pose values you pass (`solvedModel(poses)`,
  sweep joint, IK) are driven; the other loop mates are solved. Drive as many
  joints as the loop's mobility (rank of the closure Jacobian) — `solve_mates`
  reports `loop.mobility[]` with `mobility`, the spatial Grübler count,
  `drivenDof` and `independent` (a valid set of joints to drive). Over-driven
  loops whose values disagree fail with `kinematic.loop.mobility-mismatch`.
- **Author the as-built pose closed** (mate `pose` values or connector
  origins that already assemble), away from a flat or straight pose. Capture-
  time poses are the seed, never driven.
- **Continuation.** A solve far from the as-built pose marches there in ≤ 5°
  steps; sweeps (`checkSweptCollision`, `motion-load`, IK) seed each pose from
  the previous one. The mechanism stays in the assembly mode it was modeled
  in. Crossing a singular configuration stops the sweep with
  `kinematic.loop.branch-flip` (joint + pose) — it never switches silently.
  A pose the loop cannot reach stops it with `kinematic.loop.lockup`.

description: kernelCAD MCP server (kernelcad mcp) — introspect a running model, list features, run edit ops, fetch diagnostic codes. Use when you need to inspect a live model dynamically rather than re-evaluate from source.
---

# kernelCAD — MCP companion

## When to load this skill

Load when `kernelcad mcp` is available and you need to inspect or edit a live model without re-running the full CLI on every change. The MCP server exposes dynamic introspection tools that operate on evaluated in-memory state.

### Sandbox mode

If the server's `initialize` instructions start with `kernelCAD SANDBOX MODE is ON`
(the server was started with `kernelcad mcp --sandbox` or `KERNELCAD_SANDBOX=1`),
three rules apply. Every path you pass, and every path a script reads, must
resolve inside the named workspace: use workspace-relative paths. All outbound
network is refused. Network modes return `cli.sandbox-network-denied`:
`import_step` url/upload, `fetch_part`/`find_part` `partsBaseUrl` or
`model.url`, `trace_from_image` with an http(s) image, `render_preview`
`base_url`, a URL `environment`, and the Studio selection tools.
`send_to_printer` returns `cli.sandbox-command-refused`. Switch to the offline
input (`content_base64`, a workspace file, a bundled HDRI preset) and do not
retry the same call. Paths that escape return `cli.sandbox-path-denied` and
name the argument.

## MCP tool surface

When you have `kernelcad mcp` available, use the MCP tools for dynamic introspection rather than re-running the CLI. The MCP server exposes the current tool registry, including:

### Point-cloud analysis

- `fit_plane({ points })` — fit an orthogonal least-squares plane to at least three non-collinear XYZ triples (up to 100,000). Returns the centroid, deterministic unit normal, signed orthogonal residual per point, RMS residual and maximum absolute residual. Pass points parsed by the caller from a scan or mesh; this tool estimates parameters only and does not parse files or create a surface body.
- `load_scan_reference` / `fit_model_to_scan` — read a PLY or XYZ cloud as a non-solid reference and compare a parametric bounding box. Details are in the tool list below. The cloud is not drawn in Studio.

### Evaluation and introspection


- `evaluate_script({ file? code?, dryRun? })` — pass/fail + featureCount + diagnostics + `sceneSummary` (`valid`, `volume` in mm³, BREP `faceCount`, conservative world bounding `size: [x,y,z]` in mm); plus a `parts` summary `{ count, names }` when the scene is assembly-built (absent for single-shape / non-assembly scripts). `dryRun: true` is the fast iteration mode: transpile + capture + capture-light checks without building solids, DFM gates, or meshing — milliseconds instead of seconds. A dry run catches script throws, capture-time API misuse, and assembly validity-gate failures, but NOT lowering failures (failed booleans, oversized fillets) or `dfmSpec` diagnostics, and it leaves the active session untouched — finish with a full `evaluate_script` before using session-dependent tools. A model with moving joints or motion intent (an animation track, `mechanicalJoint`, transmission) also gets `mechanismSummary` — `{ verdict, maxLevel, statement, checked, skipped, failures, loopMobility? }` (`maxLevel`: `error` broken, `warning` not checked, `ok` checked). `loopMobility`, when present for closed loops, gives the solver's loop names, coordinate count, closure-Jacobian rank and mobility per sampled pose. The verdict also fails an animation key that drives a joint past its limits (`kinematic.pose.out-of-limits`), a closed loop that does not close (`assembly.mate.over-constrained` / `assembly.solver.did-not-converge`, naming the mate) and a loop mate that comes apart at a swept pose (`mechanism.mate-unsatisfied`); a moving DOF with no limits is listed in `skipped` (range not checked), not failed. Quote `statement`: `Motion checked` says what ran, `Motion not checked` is not a pass (say it was not checked), `Mechanism broken` names the joint. An animated param or drive on a `fastened` joint fails as `mechanism.motion-on-fixed-joint`: make that joint revolute/prismatic and pass the param as its `pose`; never animate a transform of a fastened part's geometry with that param. Studio shows the same verdict as a badge; saving is never blocked by it.
- `diff_scripts({ baseFile? baseCode?, file? code? })` — structured geometric delta between a baseline script and a revision. Returns per-part `added`/`removed`/`renamed`/`changed` (volume mm³ + exact bbox deltas; numbers match `inspect({ of: 'part-stats' })`), interference totals per side + `deltaMm3` with per-pair detail, mate-graph changes (type, connectors, pose, limits, `coupleMates` coupling), and param changes (value/min/max). Single-shape scripts diff as one `(root)` pseudo-part. Use after editing a script to verify exactly what changed physically before re-rendering; read-only, never touches the active session.
- `diff_geometry({ baseFile? baseCode?, file? code?, params?, render? })` — the deeper sibling of `diff_scripts`, for when a volume/bbox delta is ambiguous: a boss that grew and a pocket that deepened report the same |ΔV|, and a part that only moved reports ΔV = 0. The revised side is either another script (`file`/`code`) or the SAME script re-lowered with `params` overrides (declared `param()` name → new value — the one-script form a parameter sweep asks for). Bodies pair by name, falling back to declaration-order positional pairing; leftovers land in `unmatched` and raise `diff.body.unmatched`. Per matched body: `addedMm3` = volume(revised − base), `removedMm3` = volume(base − revised), `commonMm3` = volume(base ∩ revised), exact bbox with min/max/extent deltas, face/edge/hole count deltas, `maxDeviationMm` (two-sided discrete Hausdorff distance), and a `verdict` — `identical` | `moved` | `resized` | `topology-changed` (precedence: topology-changed > resized > moved > identical). **Branch on the verdict; cite the numbers.** Each body also has `faces` — WHICH faces changed: `{ added, removed, modified, unchangedCount }`, each entry `{ surfaceType, areaMm2, center, normal?, axis?, radiusMm?, ref? }` (`ref` is a stable `@kc[...]` face ref on the revised model when the face has a lineage name); modified entries add `{ before, after, offsetMm, change: 'moved' | 'resized' | 'reshaped', matchedBy: 'lineage' | 'geometry' }`. Faces pair by lineage first (so a translated box reports six moved faces), then by geometry (same type, parallel normal/axis, nearest centroid); lists are capped at 50 with `truncated` and true totals. `summary.text` says it in plain language, e.g. `Body '(root)' topology-changed: 1 face added (cylinder r=3 at (20, 20, 3)), 2 faces resized (…)`. `{ render: true }` also writes an overlay PNG — added green, removed red, unchanged material as a translucent ghost — through the `render_preview` pipeline; the scene itself is a re-runnable `diff-overlay.kcad.ts` over lossless BREP sidecars in `render.out_dir`. It fails open: the numeric diff is returned either way, with `render.error` naming what the render pipeline needs. Read-only. `diff_scripts` sets `deeperDiffAvailable` when its own numbers are not enough to say what physically changed; follow that pointer here instead of reaching for a render.
- `inspect({ of: 'features', file? code? })` — array of feature summaries (kind/id/params/inputs)
- `inspect({ of: 'assemblies', file? code? })` — captured assembly intent: assemblies, parts, named connectors, fixed connections, joints, and aggregate models
- `inspect({ of: 'assembly', file? | code?, assembly? })` — physical assembly inventory for agents: named parts, bboxes, explicitly assigned engineering `material` (from `assembly.part(..., { material })`), connectors, mates (a mate driven by `coupleMates` carries `coupling: { source, ratio, offset? }`), mechanical review facts, disconnected solids, `unexplainedGeometry`, and a next-action prompt. `componentCount` is a disconnected-mesh diagnostic only; it is not a stable cell/region identity and cannot be assigned an independent material. Assign separate materials by modeling separate named assembly parts. Run this before accepting visually suspicious mechanisms; random/floating geometry must be repaired or explicitly justified by the original prompt.
- `inspect({ of: 'step', file })` — inspect a STEP file directly, without evaluating a script (`{ file }` is required; no `{ code }` mode): solid tree (index + best-effort name), per-solid exact bounding box + volume + face count, and detected cylindrical holes (axis origin + direction, diameter, depth, blind/through; co-axial seam-split faces merge into one bore). A bore whose wall is breached (a slot, pocket, or nearby fillet/chamfer runs into it) is still reported, flagged `partial: true` with `angularCoverageDeg`; the report then says `holeDetection: 'heuristic'` (also when an ambiguous concave cylinder was left out) — treat those holes as candidates to confirm with a render or section. `'exact'` means every concave cylinder was a full bore or clearly a fillet/slot end. `depthMm` is the cylindrical wall length: a mouth chamfer/fillet shortens it. Run this before placing an imported vendor part — find mounting-hole positions and verify the part-local frame from exact geometry instead of measuring renders. CLI equivalent: `kernelcad inspect step <file.step>`.
- `inspect({ of: 'shape', file? code?, feature_id? })` — volume/surfaceArea/bbox of a feature (default: last)
- `inspect({ of: 'topology', file? code?, feature_id? })` — canonical face names + edge count
- `inspect({ of: 'face-edges', file? code?, feature_id?, face_name })` — boundary edges of a face (centroid, length, isClosed)
- `inspect({ of: 'edges', file? code?, feature_id? })` — enumerate all edges (index, centroid, length, isClosed)
- `inspect({ of: 'faces', file? code?, feature_id? })` — enumerate all faces with area and centroid
- `inspect_nurbs({ file? code?, feature_id? })` — read captured NURBS data from a `nurbsCurve`/`spline3d` feature: degree, knots and multiplicities, poles, weights, parameter range, `rational` (weights not all equal), `uniformWeights` (all equal), and `hasNonUnitWeights` (any differs from 1). This reports authored curve data, not post-operation B-rep edge/face extraction; surfaces and blends are not supported.
- `apply_surface_blend({ code, shape_binding, operation?, radius?, distance?, selector?, continuity? })` — insert a `Shape.fillet(...)` or `Shape.chamfer(...)` line before a direct top-level `return shape_binding`, return that blend result, evaluate the patched code, and return `new_code` plus diagnostics and scene summary. `selector` uses the existing `EdgeSelector` conventions (`@kc[...]` edge ref/query, an array of selected stable edge refs, or `{ face: canonical name | face label | FaceQuery descriptor }`); omit it to affect all sharp edges. Fillets accept `continuity: 'G1' | 'G2'` through the existing public API; chamfers use `distance`. This authors and evaluates the geometry operation. It does not extract blend-surface NURBS poles; that still requires kernel surface extraction.
- `inspect({ of: 'face-labels', file? code?, feature_id? })` — canonical face names resolvable on a feature
- `query({ mode: 'lineage', file? code?, feature_id, ref })` — walk the HistoryMap chain that produced a named face/edge ref; returns `{ chain, usedFallback }`.

### Shared local Studio selection

- `get_selection({ studio_url, session })` — read the primary face/edge pick and the complete multi-selection (`selections`) from the same local Studio session. The Studio URL is a local HTTP origin; acquire `session` from `GET /__kernelcad/session?script=<path>` for the script open in Studio. A pick has `{ shapeIndex, kind, id, featureId }`; edge picks also include a stable `stableId` and an operation-ready `ref`, such as `@kc[box_1/edge/s0123456789abcdef]`. Edge IDs fingerprint curve type, length, and nine 3D samples quantized to `1e-6` model units, independent of edge orientation and traversal order. They survive re-evaluation while geometry is unchanged; ambiguous matches are rejected. For a selected-edge fillet or chamfer, pass the edge refs from `selections` to `apply_surface_blend.selector`. Face picks keep their existing signature-based remap. The tools currently support local Studio sessions, not hosted sessions.
- `set_selection({ studio_url, session, model_generation, selection, selections? })` — replace the primary viewer selection and optionally the full face/edge multi-selection, or clear with `selection: null` and `selections: []`. Pass the model generation from the latest `get_selection` response. Stable edge IDs are checked against the current mesh; stale generations and mismatched refs are rejected. Studio updates its existing highlights on the next sync cycle. These tools change selection only, not geometry, and currently support local Studio sessions, not hosted sessions.

### Diagnostics

- `why_did_this_fail({ file? code?, feature_id?, diagnostic? })` — walk the upstream chain of a failing feature; returns each upstream feature's id/kind/health/diagnostics in topological order (per-code hints already inline on every diagnostic). Use when `code` is `recompute.input.missing` to find the root cause. Also returns `trace` (every feature joined to its call site, AST node range, inputs and dependents), `repairRegion` (the only lines an edit may touch), and ordered `candidates` with real patches — or `candidateStatus: 'no-automatic-candidate'` when no mechanical fix exists.
- `repair_script({ file? code?, diagnostic?, strategy?, max_attempts? })` — apply those candidates one at a time, re-evaluate after each, and keep the first that clears the diagnostic without new errors. `strategy`: `'try-all'` (default), `'apply-first'`, `'dry-run'`. Returns `new_code` + `diff` + before/after health maps. Refuses any patch outside `repairRegion` (`tool.repair.out-of-region`). Load `kernelcad-repair` for the full loop.
- `lookup_diagnostics({})` — return the full diagnostic catalogue with hint templates, structured next-actions, and per-code metadata (one-shot; useful at session start to pre-populate retry strategies).
- `lookup_api({})` — full curated API surface (globals, Shape methods, Sketch methods, constrained-sketch capability)
- `lookup_cookbook({ query, k? })` — retrieve up to k canonical pattern snippets ranked by BM25; returns `{ ok, hits[] }`. Empty hits is a valid success ("no canonical pattern; proceed without cookbook help").
- `execute_cookbook({ id?, query?, openInStudio?, dryRun? })` — **prefer this after `lookup_cookbook` for industry demos when you need evaluate + optional Studio in one step**; empty lookup is not a stop (freehand-author instead). Resolves by `id` or BM25 top hit (same as lookup), runs `evaluate_script` on the snippet body (bounded vendor timeouts), returns `{ ok, cookbookId, title, evaluate, openInStudio?, executionId, code?, stage?, error? }` with concrete `stage`: `resolve` | `evaluate` | `open_in_studio`. `openInStudio:true` (default false) publishes via `open_in_studio` after a green full evaluate on hosted MCP. **`dryRun:true` is NOT evidence** the cookbook builds a solid — finish with `dryRun:false` (default) before claiming success or opening Studio.
- `import_step({ url? | upload? | content_base64?, file_name?, format?, output_dir?, name?, allow_open? })` — start from the user's own STEP/STL in chat. Give a public https URL, a ChatGPT attachment (`upload`, declared via `openai/fileParams`), or base64 bytes (max 50 MB). Writes the file and a starter `<name>.kcad.ts` (`lib.fromSTEP` / `lib.fromSTL` as the base body), evaluates it, and returns `{ ok, format, model_path, script_path, code, bbox }`. Pass the returned script path as `{ file }` to other tools.
- `blockout_assembly({ name?, parts: [{ name, bboxMm, positionMm, rotationDeg?, anchors? }], connections? })` — turn a plain list of parts (bbox `[x,y,z]` and lower-corner `positionMm` in mm, optional `rotationDeg` about Z or XYZ Euler, optional named `anchors: [{ name, positionMm }]` in assembly coordinates) into an evaluable placeholder assembly script and return `{ ok, part_count, connection_count, script, warnings }`. Each part is a corner-anchored box with built-in connectors (`origin`, `bbox_center`, `bbox_x_min`..`bbox_z_max`) plus its anchors (emitted as `anchor_<name>`). `connections: [{ from, to }]` use `"part.anchor"` references and become `fastened` mates that express connectivity intent only. The tool reads no files, cuts nothing and generates no wire geometry; route real wires or tubes with sweeps along a path, and refine the boxes with `add_part` / `add_feature`. Use it when a layout, spreadsheet or another tool hands you part sizes and positions; for one part at a time use `add_part`.
- `estimate_cost({ file|code, process?, material?, quantity? })` — labelled offline USD heuristic for a fabricated part or assembly. `process` is `'3d-print' | 'cnc' | 'sheet-cut'`; omit it to compare all three. Reuses volume, bounding box, and any `assembly.part` material, FabProcess, and StockSpec. Returns `currencyLabel: 'USD estimate'`, a material + setup + cycle breakdown, confidence, and key drivers. Not a supplier quote. Purchased catalog parts are skipped. No solid returns `estimate.no-geometry`.
- `analyze_tolerance_stack({ contributors } | { file|code, chain, requirement? })` — labelled 1D worst-case and RSS stack. Contributors are `{ id, nominal_mm, upper_mm, lower_mm, sense: '+' | '-' }`. `requirement` is `{ kind: 'gap' | 'clearance' | 'length', min_mm?, max_mm? }`. `chain` names `shape.dimension` ids or labels; a chain `tol` overrides the declaration. A missing tolerance returns `cli.invalid-args` (ISO 2768 is not applied). RSS is the independent ±3σ band, using each half-width `(upper−lower)/2` as the ±3σ proxy. `requirement.pass` follows the worst case. This is a 1D arithmetic stack, not a full GD&T capability study. `shape.tolerance` frames and `require()` clearances stay on `verify({ check: 'requirements' })`.
- `load_scan_reference({ file | data, units?, max_points? })` — read an ASCII PLY, little-endian binary PLY, or XYZ/XYZRGB cloud as a non-BREP reference. Coordinates are millimetres unless `units` is `m` or `in`. Returns `point_count`, `bbox` `{ min, max, size }`, and `centroid`. Clouds above `max_points` (default and cap 200000) are stride-downsampled and flagged; the bbox still uses every parsed point. `binary_big_endian` and list vertex properties are refused by format name. Booleans on the scan are refused. `mesh_to_features` and `lib.fromSTL` still promote meshes; they do not consume this cloud. Studio does not draw it.
- `fit_model_to_scan({ file | code, scan_file | scan_data | scan_bbox, units?, requirement? })` — measure the script with the existing bounding box and compare it to a scan file or to `{ min_mm, max_mm }` (`min` / `max` from a prior `load_scan_reference` bbox are accepted). Returns `translate_mm` (model center onto the scan center), `scale.per_axis`, `scale.uniform` (largest isotropic factor that stays inside the scan; apply it about the model center, then translate), and `clearance_mm` (scan size minus model size; positive means the unscaled model extent fits inside). `requirement.min_clearance_mm` sets pass/fail. - `resolve_metric_thread` — ISO 261 coarse designation from a hole diameter in millimetres. 12 mm is M12x1.75. kind is nominal (default, within 0.05 mm), tap_drill (D − P within 0.1 mm; 5 mm is M6), or auto (nominal first, then tap drill). It does not cut geometry.
- `split_keep_parts` — keep the overlap and both leftovers from `shape.split`. Returns `parts` (`name`, volume_mm3, `bbox`), `ok` and `diagnostics`. `subtract` / `intersect` / `union` still return one Shape. Face refs that the cut splits stay ambiguous.
- `run_flight({ file|code, study?, motor?, aero?, launch?, recovery?, dry_mass_kg?, min_stability_cal?, series?: 'json'|'csv'|'none', sample_dt_s?, animation_speed?, output_dir? })` — model-rocket flight study: runs the script's `arm.flightStudy(...)` (call fields override it) or an inline study. - `dfm_review({ file|code, processes?, nozzle_mm?, max_overhang_deg?, max_bridge_mm?, printer?, build_direction?, tool_diameter_mm?, approach_axes?, max_undercut_area_mm2?, min_bend_radius_ratio?, hole_to_bend_thicknesses?, hole_to_edge_thicknesses?, min_flange_thicknesses?, pull_direction?, min_draft_deg?, min_wall_mm?, max_wall_mm?, max_wall_ratio?, min_radius_mm? })` — manufacturability checklist with no `dfmSpec` needed; `processes` is any of `'fdm' | 'cnc' | 'sheet-metal' | 'injection-molding'` (default `['fdm', 'cnc']`). Outcomes are `pass`, `fail`, or `not-checked`: a checked failure wins over incomplete checks; without a failure, any missing requested analysis or unmeasured required rule yields `not-checked`; warnings remain `warn` and do not fail a completed review. Sheet metal (a `sheetMetal(...).bend(...)` part; thickness read from the model, anything else returns `sheet.not-sheet-metal: not-checked`): bend radius ≥ t, hole-to-bend ≥ 2.5 × t + R, hole-to-edge ≥ 2 × t, flange ≥ 4 × t, located on the flat pattern. Injection molding (the `dfmSpec({ process: 'moulding' })` engine; two-part mold along ±`pull_direction`, default `+z`): draft ≥ 1° (face refs are optional and omitted when unique resolvable lineage is unavailable), walls ≥ 1 mm (fail) and ≤ 4 mm plus a max/min ratio (warn), undercuts neither half releases, internal corners under R0.5 (warn). A script's `dfmSpec` fdm / moulding settings are the defaults; call options win. Returns `{ ok, verdict?: pass|fail|not-checked, checks: [{ id (rule key), process, part, source, status: pass|fail|warn|not-checked, summary, value?, limit?, unit?, op?, tolerance?, refs? }] }`. Tolerance uses the same unit as value and limit, is inclusive, and defaults to zero: for `>=`, pass when `value + tolerance >= limit`; for `<=`, pass when `value - tolerance <= limit`. `ok` reports invocation/model/analysis execution, not manufacturability: checked failures can return `ok: true`; input or model-evaluation errors return `ok: false` with no manufacturing verdict.
- `dfm_fix_recheck({ file|code, process? | processes?, finding_id?, diagnostic_code?, material?, ...same review options })` — one bounded fix, then the same `dfm_review`. Applies at most one edit: an existing fillet radius up to the named corner limit, a `shell()` thickness up to the minimum wall plus 0.01 mm, or a `draft()` angle up to the minimum draft. Sharp corners, undrafted faces, and dimensions that are not that feature argument come back as suggestions and are not edited. `material` is recorded and does

# kernelCAD — MCP companion

## When to load this skill

Load when `kernelcad mcp` is available and you need to inspect or edit a live model without re-running the full CLI on every change. The MCP server exposes dynamic introspection tools that operate on evaluated in-memory state.

### Sandbox mode

If the server's `initialize` instructions start with `kernelCAD SANDBOX MODE is ON`
(the server was started with `kernelcad mcp --sandbox` or `KERNELCAD_SANDBOX=1`),
three rules apply. Every path you pass, and every path a script reads, must
resolve inside the named workspace: use workspace-relative paths. All outbound
network is refused. Network modes return `cli.sandbox-network-denied`:
`import_step` url/upload, `fetch_part`/`find_part` `partsBaseUrl` or
`model.url`, `trace_from_image` with an http(s) image, `render_preview`
`base_url`, a URL `environment`, and the Studio selection tools.
`send_to_printer` returns `cli.sandbox-command-refused`. Switch to the offline
input (`content_base64`, a workspace file, a bundled HDRI preset) and do not
retry the same call. Paths that escape return `cli.sandbox-path-denied` and
name the argument.

## MCP tool surface

When you have `kernelcad mcp` available, use the MCP tools for dynamic introspection rather than re-running the CLI. The MCP server exposes the current tool registry, including:

### Point-cloud analysis

- `fit_plane({ points })` — fit an orthogonal least-squares plane to at least three non-collinear XYZ triples (up to 100,000). Returns the centroid, deterministic unit normal, signed orthogonal residual per point, RMS residual and maximum absolute residual. Pass points parsed by the caller from a scan or mesh; this tool estimates parameters only and does not parse files or create a surface body.
- `load_scan_reference` / `fit_model_to_scan` — read a PLY or XYZ cloud as a non-solid reference and compare a parametric bounding box. Details are in the tool list below. The cloud is not drawn in Studio.

### Evaluation and introspection


- `evaluate_script({ file? code?, dryRun? })` — pass/fail + featureCount + diagnostics + `sceneSummary` (`valid`, `volume` in mm³, BREP `faceCount`, conservative world bounding `size: [x,y,z]` in mm); plus a `parts` summary `{ count, names }` when the scene is assembly-built (absent for single-shape / non-assembly scripts). `dryRun: true` is the fast iteration mode: transpile + capture + capture-light checks without building solids, DFM gates, or meshing — milliseconds instead of seconds. A dry run catches script throws, capture-time API misuse, and assembly validity-gate failures, but NOT lowering failures (failed booleans, oversized fillets) or `dfmSpec` diagnostics, and it leaves the active session untouched — finish with a full `evaluate_script` before using session-dependent tools. A model with moving joints or motion intent (an animation track, `mechanicalJoint`, transmission) also gets `mechanismSummary` — `{ verdict, maxLevel, statement, checked, skipped, failures, loopMobility? }` (`maxLevel`: `error` broken, `warning` not checked, `ok` checked). `loopMobility`, when present for closed loops, gives the solver's loop names, coordinate count, closure-Jacobian rank and mobility per sampled pose. The verdict also fails an animation key that drives a joint past its limits (`kinematic.pose.out-of-limits`), a closed loop that does not close (`assembly.mate.over-constrained` / `assembly.solver.did-not-converge`, naming the mate) and a loop mate that comes apart at a swept pose (`mechanism.mate-unsatisfied`); a moving DOF with no limits is listed in `skipped` (range not checked), not failed. Quote `statement`: `Motion checked` says what ran, `Motion not checked` is not a pass (say it was not checked), `Mechanism broken` names the joint. An animated param or drive on a `fastened` joint fails as `mechanism.motion-on-fixed-joint`: make that joint revolute/prismatic and pass the param as its `pose`; never animate a transform of a fastened part's geometry with that param. Studio shows the same verdict as a badge; saving is never blocked by it.
- `diff_scripts({ baseFile? baseCode?, file? code? })` — structured geometric delta between a baseline script and a revision. Returns per-part `added`/`removed`/`renamed`/`changed` (volume mm³ + exact bbox deltas; numbers match `inspect({ of: 'part-stats' })`), interference totals per side + `deltaMm3` with per-pair detail, mate-graph changes (type, connectors, pose, limits, `coupleMates` coupling), and param changes (value/min/max). It fails open: the numeric diff is returned either way, with `render.error` naming what the render pipeline needs. Read-only. `diff_scripts` sets `deeperDiffAvailable` when its own numbers are not enough to say what physically changed; follow that pointer here instead of reaching for a render.

- `why_did_this_fail({ file? code?, feature_id?, diagnostic? })` — walk the upstream chain of a failing feature; returns each upstream feature's id/kind/health/diagnostics in topological order (per-code hints already inline on every diagnostic). Use when `code` is `recompute.input.missing` to find the root cause. Also returns `trace` (every feature joined to its call site, AST node range, inputs and dependents), `repairRegion` (the only lines an edit may touch), and ordered `candidates` with real patches — or `candidateStatus: 'no-automatic-candidate'` when no mechanical fix exists.
- `repair_script({ file? code?, diagnostic?, strategy?, max_attempts? })` — apply those candidates one at a time, re-evaluate after each, and keep the first that clears the diagnostic without new errors. `strategy`: `'try-all'` (default), `'apply-first'`, `'dry-run'`. Returns `new_code` + `diff` + before/after health maps. Refuses any patch outside `repairRegion` (`tool.repair.out-of-region`). Load `kernelcad-repair` for the full loop.
- `lookup_diagnostics({})` — return the full diagnostic catalogue with hint templates, structured next-actions, and per-code metadata (one-shot; useful at session start to pre-populate retry strategies).
- `lookup_api({})` — full curated API surface (globals, Shape methods, Sketch methods, constrained-sketch capability)
- `lookup_cookbook({ query, k? })` — retrieve up to k canonical pattern snippets ranked by BM25; returns `{ ok, hits[] }`. Empty hits is a valid success ("no canonical pattern; proceed without cookbook help").
- `execute_cookbook({ id?, query?, openInStudio?, dryRun? })` — **prefer this after `lookup_cookbook` for industry demos when you need evaluate + optional Studio in one step**; empty lookup is not a stop (freehand-author instead). Resolves by `id` or BM25 top hit (same as lookup), runs `evaluate_script` on the snippet body (bounded vendor timeouts), returns `{ ok, cookbookId, title, evaluate, openInStudio?, executionId, code?, stage?, error? }` with concrete `stage`: `resolve` | `evaluate` | `open_in_studio`. `openInStudio:true` (default false) publishes via `open_in_studio` after a green full evaluate on hosted MCP. **`dryRun:true` is NOT evidence** the cookbook builds a solid — finish with `dryRun:false` (default) before claiming success or opening Studio.
- `import_step({ url? | upload? | content_base64?, file_name?, format?, output_dir?, name?, allow_open? })` — start from the user's own STEP/STL in chat. Give a public https URL, a ChatGPT attachment (`upload`, declared via `openai/fileParams`), or base64 bytes (max 50 MB). Writes the file and a starter `<name>.kcad.ts` (`lib.fromSTEP` / `lib.fromSTL` as the base body), evaluates it, and returns `{ ok, format, model_path, script_path, code, bbox }`. Pass the returned script path as `{ file }` to other tools.
- `blockout_assembly({ name?, parts: [{ name, bboxMm, positionMm, rotationDeg?, anchors? }], connections? })` — turn a plain list of parts (bbox `[x,y,z]` and lower-corner `positionMm` in mm, optional `rotationDeg` about Z or XYZ Euler, optional named `anchors: [{ name, positionMm }]` in assembly coordinates) into an evaluable placeholder assembly script and return `{ ok, part_count, connection_count, script, warnings }`. Each part is a corner-anchored box with built-in connectors (`origin`, `bbox_center`, `bbox_x_min`..`bbox_z_max`) plus its anchors (emitted as `anchor_<name>`). `connections: [{ from, to }]` use `"part.anchor"` references and become `fastened` mates that express connectivity intent only. The tool reads no files, cuts nothing and generates no wire geometry; route real wires or tubes with sweeps along a path, and refine the boxes with `add_part` / `add_feature`. Use it when a layout, spreadsheet or another tool hands you part sizes and positions; for one part at a time use `add_part`.
- `estimate_cost({ file|code, process?, material?, quantity? })` — labelled offline USD heuristic for a fabricated part or assembly. `process` is `'3d-print' | 'cnc' | 'sheet-cut'`; omit it to compare all three. Reuses volume, bounding box, and any `assembly.part` material, FabProcess, and StockSpec. Returns `currencyLabel: 'USD estimate'`, a material + setup + cycle breakdown, confidence, and key drivers. Not a supplier quote. Purchased catalog parts are skipped. No solid returns `estimate.no-geometry`.
- `analyze_tolerance_stack({ contributors } | { file|code, chain, requirement? })` — labelled 1D worst-case and RSS stack. Contributors are `{ id, nominal_mm, upper_mm, lower_mm, sense: '+' | '-' }`. `requirement` is `{ kind: 'gap' | 'clearance' | 'length', min_mm?, max_mm? }`. `chain` names `shape.dimension` ids or labels; a chain `tol` overrides the declaration. A missing tolerance returns `cli.invalid-args` (ISO 2768 is not applied). RSS is the independent ±3σ band, using each half-width `(upper−lower)/2` as the ±3σ proxy. `requirement.pass` follows the worst case. This is a 1D arithmetic stack, not a full GD&T capability study. `shape.tolerance` frames and `require()` clearances stay on `verify({ check: 'requirements' })`.
- `load_scan_reference({ file | data, units?, max_points? })` — read an ASCII PLY, little-endian binary PLY, or XYZ/XYZRGB cloud as a non-BREP reference. Coordinates are millimetres unless `units` is `m` or `in`. Returns `point_count`, `bbox` `{ min, max, size }`, and `centroid`. Clouds above `max_points` (default and cap 200000) are stride-downsampled and flagged; the bbox still uses every parsed point. `binary_big_endian` and list vertex properties are refused by format name. Booleans on the scan are refused. `mesh_to_features` and `lib.fromSTL` still promote meshes; they do not consume this cloud. Studio does not draw it.
- `fit_model_to_scan({ file | code, scan_file | scan_data | scan_bbox, units?, requirement? })` — measure the script with the existing bounding box and compare it to a scan file or to `{ min_mm, max_mm }` (`min` / `max` from a prior `load_scan_reference` bbox are accepted). Returns `translate_mm` (model center onto the scan center), `scale.per_axis`, `scale.uniform` (largest isotropic factor that stays inside the scan; apply it about the model center, then translate), and `clearance_mm` (scan size minus model size; positive means the unscaled model extent fits inside). `requirement.min_clearance_mm` sets pass/fail. The scan is not booleaned into the solid.
- `resolve_metric_thread` — ISO 261 coarse designation from a hole diameter in millimetres. 12 mm is M12x1.75. kind is nominal (default, within 0.05 mm), tap_drill (D − P within 0.1 mm; 5 mm is M6), or auto (nominal first, then tap drill). A clearance bore such as 13.5 mm is refused; use clearanceFitForHoleDiameter. In a script, `hole({ diameter: 12, thread: true })` or `metricThreadFromDiameter(12)` records the same coarse pitch. It does not cut geometry.
- `split_keep_parts` — keep the overlap and both leftovers from `shape.split`. Pass `{ file | code }` that returns the split, or `{ body_code, tool_code }` (Shape expressions) which the tool wraps as `body.split(tool)`. `keep` is `parts` (default), `intersection`, a_only, or b_only, and it applies only on the wrapper. Parts are named `intersection` (A ∩ B), a_only (A − B) and b_only (B − A); a fragment at or below 1e-6 mm³ is omitted, so disjoint operands return two parts. Returns `parts` (`name`, volume_mm3, `bbox`), `ok` and `diagnostics`. `subtract` / `intersect` / `union` still return one Shape. Face refs that the cut splits stay ambiguous.
- `run_flight({ file|code, study?, motor?, aero?, launch?, recovery?, dry_mass_kg?, min_stability_cal?, series?: 'json'|'csv'|'none', sample_dt_s?, animation_speed?, output_dir? })` — model-rocket flight study: runs the script's `arm.flightStudy(...)` (call fields override it) or an inline study. Mass and CG from the parts, Barrowman CP and static margin (calibers) from the nose / fin geometry, RK4 point-mass trajectory with ISA, rail, wind and parachutes. Returns `summary` (apogeeM, apogeeTimeS, maxSpeedMs, maxAccelMs2, railExitSpeedMs, descentRateMs, landingTimeS, stability, motor, events, assumptions), `series` (t, x, z, v, vz, a, a_axial, p_static_hpa, temp_c, mass, thrust, chute) and an `animation` track for `animationView`. `ok` is false on `flight.stability.below-min` / `flight.stability.unresolved` / `flight.study.part-unresolved` / `flight.mass.unavailable` / `flight.sim.no-liftoff`.
- `dfm_review({ file|code, processes?, nozzle_mm?, max_overhang_deg?, max_bridge_mm?, printer?, build_direction?, tool_diameter_mm?, approach_axes?, max_undercut_area_mm2?, min_bend_radius_ratio?, hole_to_bend_thicknesses?, hole_to_edge_thicknesses?, min_flange_thicknesses?, pull_direction?, min_draft_deg?, min_wall_mm?, max_wall_mm?, max_wall_ratio?, min_radius_mm? })` — manufacturability checklist with no `dfmSpec` needed; `processes` is any of `'fdm' | 'cnc' | 'sheet-metal' | 'injection-molding'` (default `['fdm', 'cnc']`). Outcomes are `pass`, `fail`, or `not-checked`: a checked failure wins over incomplete checks; without a failure, any missing requested analysis or unmeasured required rule yields `not-checked`; warnings remain `warn` and do not fail a completed review. Sheet metal (a `sheetMetal(...).bend(...)` part; thickness read from the model, anything else returns `sheet.not-sheet-metal: not-checked`): bend radius ≥ t, hole-to-bend ≥ 2.5 × t + R, hole-to-edge ≥ 2 × t, flange ≥ 4 × t, located on the flat pattern. Injection molding (the `dfmSpec({ process: 'moulding' })` engine; two-part mold along ±`pull_direction`, default `+z`): draft ≥ 1° (face refs are optional and omitted when unique resolvable lineage is unavailable), walls ≥ 1 mm (fail) and ≤ 4 mm plus a max/min ratio (warn), undercuts neither half releases, internal corners under R0.5 (warn). A script's `dfmSpec` fdm / moulding settings are the defaults; call options win. Returns `{ ok, verdict?: pass|fail|not-checked, checks: [{ id (rule key), process, part, source, status: pass|fail|warn|not-checked, summary, value?, limit?, unit?, op?, tolerance?, refs? }] }`. Tolerance uses the same unit as value and limit, is inclusive, and defaults to zero: for `>=`, pass when `value + tolerance >= limit`; for `<=`, pass when `value - tolerance <= limit`. `ok` reports invocation/model/analysis execution, not manufacturability: checked failures can return `ok: true`; input or model-evaluation errors return `ok: false` with no manufacturing verdict.
- `dfm_fix_recheck({ file|code, process? | processes?, finding_id?, diagnostic_code?, material?, ...same review options })` — one bounded fix, then the same `dfm_review`. Applies at most one edit: an existing fillet radius up to the named corner limit, a `shell()` thickness up to the minimum wall plus 0.01 mm, or a `draft()` angle up to the minimum draft. Sharp corners, undrafted faces, and dimensions that are not that feature argument come back as suggestions and are not edited. `material` is recorded and does not change the gates. Pass `process` or `processes`, not both. Before/after findings retain `value`, `limit`, `unit`, `op`, and the comparison `tolerance` when present; absent tolerance means zero.
